As a neuroscientist who studies raccoons and rats, I see the viral story of Jimothy the raccoon as a compelling tale of an animal overcoming disability and surviving in the wild.

Jimothy, the unique-looking raccoon living in Seattle, became an internet celebrity over the course of a week in July 2026, thanks to a viral Instagram post that has amassed millions of views and thousands of comments cheering for the proverbial underdog. Jimothy has even been honored with a city proclamation.

Something about him was obviously different. His body and tail were unusually short, and his back was curved. Although Jimothy hasn’t been officially examined by a veterinarian, he’s thought to have a form of a rare cervical vertebral malformation called short spine syndrome. A handful of cases have been seen in dogs. These animals are born with a condition that prevents their vertebrae from fully developing. With less physical space in the body, organs are crowded into a smaller space than usual and can lead to mobility issues.

Adaptations are necessary for these animals to navigate their environments and secure the necessary resources for survival. How did Jimothy overcome the odds and emerge as a survivor?

It’s difficult to imagine how Jimothy has navigated life’s challenging terrain to survive in the wild ( TMZ via Video Elephant )

The sophisticated raccoon brain

Although it’s easy to imagine a pet dog that’s under the close care of human pet parents surviving a challenging condition such as short spine syndrome – the probability of a disabled or injured wild animal successfully living in the uncertain outdoors is a different story.

Even for healthy raccoon, it’s a challenge to survive the harrowing time of being a helpless newborn. Up to half of young kits die without emerging from the natal den. If an individual raccoon is among the fortunate to leave the den as a young adult, life’s challenges don’t stop there. Typically there are no safe zones that are reliably protected from predators.

To survive, raccoon have to be vigilant, persistent and physically agile to navigate the physical and mental challenges of life in the wild. In fact, it’s so dangerous out in the wild that many raccoon only live two to five years, even though they have the capacity to live for around 12 years in captivity.

It’s difficult to imagine how Jimothy has navigated life’s challenging terrain to survive in the wild. However, if any mammal can transcend the limitations of a disability, raccoon would be at the top of my list.

Very few studies have been conducted on the raccoon brain, but my lab’s limited research has revealed the neuroarchitecture of a complex and sophisticated brain. Raccoon have exceptionally high neuron densities, resembling those of small primates. More neurons lead to greater flexibility in behavior, a characteristic that is likely facilitating Jimothy’s survival.

My team also identified the presence of specialized and fast-conducting brain cells called von Economo neurons, which are typically located in the areas of the brain involved in emotional, social and internal processing in people.

And perhaps the neuroevolutionary pièce de résistance of the raccoon: their hands. The forepaws of raccoon are extremely dexterous and sensitive, and occupy a large portion of their brain’s motor cortex, like that of people. This investment in hand movement takes raccoon learning abilities to the next level – explaining why Toronto paid roughly US$24 million to develop raccoon-proof trash bins.

These brain capabilities likely give Jimothy some neural backup as he navigates narrow fences, climbs trees, searches for food and scopes out places for rest and refuge.

Jimothy’s mom as hero

Equally impressive as Jimothy’s own adaptations is the continuous care provided by his mother.

As challenging as the raccoon mother’s role is while raising her young, raising a kit with special needs likely requires extra energy and patience. For raccoon families, the mother is very much a single parent. Not only does she not have help from the father, but she often moves the litter to different dens to escape the threat of males potentially harming the kits. She also needs to be an efficient forager to prevent excessive time away from her vulnerable offspring.

Unlike many mammals whose young become independent soon after weaning, raccoon mothers continue taking care of their kits for much longer. Although nursing typically ends around 16 weeks, raccoon youngsters often remain with their moms for up to nine months. From weaning to leaving the natal den, maternal raccoon take their family through something like homeschooling.

About the author Kelly Lambert is a professor of behavioral neuroscience at the University of Richmond. This article is republished from The Conversation under a Creative Commons license. Read the original article.

One of my favorite examples appears in the PBS documentary “Raccoon Nation,” where a raccoon mom takes her kits on a field trip to teach them how to collapse their spines to slide past a wooden garage door. For hours, she models the behavior for her young – then observes their attempts, catching them when they fall and nudging them to try again.

It’s apparent that Jimothy’s mother was no exception to the prototypical raccoon mother – serving as nurturer, protector and teacher. Based on the videos of older Jimothy running across a field, navigating fences and exploring his world, it appears that his mom’s hard work resulted in a remarkable return on her investment.

Evolutionary perseverance

Even though the odds were stacked against Jimothy from the day of his birth, he persevered.

Jimothy is being celebrated for being different. But, in my opinion, the most interesting aspects of his story are two remarkable evolutionary achievements that all mammals share: a brain capable of adapting to an imperfect body and other life challenges, and a patient and caring mother or guardian who translates her offspring’s capabilities into abilities.

Jimothy’s mom celebrated his value long before his video debut and viral following.

News.content:

A family found human remains while cleaning out a freezer at the home of a deceased loved one, according to authorities.

The family called police in the Alaskan capital city of Juneau on Sunday night after they found what appeared to be human remains inside a chest freezer in a locked outbuilding on the property.

Juneau police said in a statement that the family had been cleaning out the home after a relative had died.

Detectives believe the remains may belong to an adult male family member. But the State Medical Examiner’s Office had not confirmed the identity as of Tuesday.

Juneau police noted that there was no missing person’s report for the man filed with the department, and it's unclear how long the remains were in the freezer.

A family has found human remains while cleaning out a freezer at the home of a deceased loved one, according to authorities ( Getty Images/iStock )

The State Medical Examiner’s Office will conduct an autopsy to determine the cause and manner of death. The Independent has reached out to the examiner’s office for comment.

“At this stage of the investigation, there is no known threat to the public,” Juneau police said. The investigation into the remains remains ongoing.

Last month, human remains were found inside the chimney of a New York City school, shocking the community.

Authorities were called to P.S./I.S. 113 Anthony J. Pranzo in Queens on June 30 after an exterminator looking for the source of a foul odor found a foot in the chimney, local outlet WABC reported at the time.

There were no students or staff in the school as they were already let out for the summer, and the building was closed for construction.

"It's just tragic, whoever it is, whatever happened, it's just really sad," resident Maggie Rosario told WABC.

New York City Public Schools called the discovery of remains “deeply upsetting and concerning” in a statement.

“We are making sure the right supports are in place for the entire school community while NYPD investigates,” the statement continued.

News.title: Ebola death toll passes 1,000 as outbreak shows no signs of slowing
News.content:
More than 1,000 people have now died in the outbreak of Ebola in the Congo, as medics struggle to curb the fastest-growing epidemic of the virus.

Dozens of deaths are being recorded each day and modelling has forecast that, in a worst case scenario, it could become the worst Ebola outbreak in history.

The outbreak, centred on the north east of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), passed the four-figure death milestone little more than two months after it was first declared.

By contrast, the worst outbreak of the haemorrhagic fever on record, which struck West Africa from 2014 to 2016, took eight months from the first case to reach 1,000 deaths. It went on to kill 11,000 people.

The latest figures from the DRC’s national public health institute show 2,536 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,033 deaths, with at least 738 patients in isolation or hospitalised.

News.title: Inflation fall a ‘false dawn’, Burnham warned
News.content:
Falling inflation is a “false dawn” for Andy Burnham, economists warned after the pace of price rises slowed in June.

The consumer prices index (CPI) fell from 2.8pc in May to 2.6pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), beating economists’ expectations of a drop to 2.7pc to mark the lowest rate in 15 months.

Lower petrol and diesel prices drove the slowdown amid a short-lived peace deal between the US and Iran, while price pressures from chocolate, oils and fats, dairy and meat also weakened.

However, economists warned a rise in household energy bills in July may already have pushed inflation back up above 3pc.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants, said: “June’s slowdown is a false dawn as it may have already been reversed this month with higher energy bills, following Ofgem’s energy price cap rise, likely to have lifted inflation above 3pc.”

July’s 13pc increase in the energy price cap has pushed typical annual bills to around £1,862, while renewed fighting between the US and Iran has reignited concerns over oil and gas supplies.

Mr Thiru said elevated inflation would create a fresh headache for John Healey, the newly appointed Chancellor, by squeezing household budgets, raising government borrowing costs and limiting his room for tax cuts or spending increases.

Charlotte O’Leary, at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “June’s peace deal and the subsequent reduction in oil and gas prices helped cool consumer price inflation. This will be a welcome figure to start the new Prime Minister’s premiership, but the honeymoon period will be short-lived.”

The Bank of England will also be watching closely as it weighs further interest rate cuts, though economists warned renewed instability in the Middle East and higher energy bills could keep inflation close to 3pc for the rest of the year.

Mr Healey said: “Falling inflation is news families want to hear, but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need.”

News.title: Russia destroys Ukraine HIV warehouse
News.content:
A Russian missile strike has destroyed $2.6m (£1.9m) worth of HIV prevention supplies in Ukraine, according to an international aid group.

The Alliance for Public Health said the attack on Sunday night near Kyiv hit a warehouse holding 62 million prevention items earmarked for Ukraine’s harm reduction programmes next year. It includes syringes, needles, alcohol wipes, and condoms intended to support more than 300,000 people.

“This is not just another strike. It is an attack on 300,000 Ukrainians who depend on HIV prevention services and on their fundamental right to health,” said Andriy Klepikov, executive director of the Alliance for Public Health.

Efforts to prevent the spread of HIV rely heavily on harm reduction programmes that supply sterile syringes and needles to people who inject drugs, alongside condoms and other supplies that help curb sexual transmission.

Mr Klepikov said the destruction of the warehouse would not immediately disrupt services, because his organisation had moved its supplies for the rest of the year out of central storage and into regional distribution centres several weeks ago as part of contingency planning.

“Russia failed,” he said, adding that the Alliance had notified international partners and appealed for urgent support to rebuild next year’s inventory.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Liverpool £100m move, Manu Kone to Man Utd, Aurelien Tchouameni update
Sports.content:

Liverpool are facing a crucial summer under new head coach Andoni Iraola and amid the backdrop of takeover talks, the former Cherries boss wants transfers.

The Reds made an approach for PSG target Maghnes Akliouche with the Parisiens unable to meet the demands of Ligue 1 rivals AS Monaco. Meanwhile, Liverpool are said to be leading the race to sign Bradley Barcola, a move which would be another blow for Arsenal, who are also rumoured to hold an interest.

There's a month to go until the Premier League returns, and with pre-season getting underway across the division, the transfer action is picking up. Chelsea completed a deal to sign England star Morgan Rogers after footing up a £117million fee to set the pace for the summer while Alejandro Garnacho has joined Aston Villa on loan.

Arsenal have welcomed Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge, but their bid to sign Newcastle star Bruno Guimaraes is stealing the headlines. The Magpies remain adamant that their captain is not for sale but could they see an Alexander Isak repeat?

Sports.title: Jermain Defoe leaves first managerial job after SIX games - 'Impossible to continue'
Sports.content:
Jermain Defoe leaves first managerial job after SIX games - 'Impossible to continue'

Jermain Defoe took his first step into management with National League side Woking at the end of March, but the ex-England's striker reign has already come to an end

View 2 Images Jermain Defoe released a statement following his exit (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

Jermain Defoe's first job as a manager has come an end after just four months. National League side Woking announced on Thursday that they'd parted ways with the Premier League icon, who said in a statement that it was 'impossible to continue'.

‌



Defoe, 43, was appointed at the end of March and guided Woking to a 10th-place finish in the fifth tier. The ex-England striker won two of his six games in charge and was expected to lead the Surrey outfit into the 2026-27 season.

‌



But Woking announced on Thursday evening that his reign has come to an end. The club said: "Woking Football Club can confirm that the club and First Team Manager Jermain Defoe have mutually agreed to part ways with immediate effect.

‌



"We would like to place on record our sincere thanks to Jermain for his contribution during his time at Woking Football Club, and we wish him every success in the future. The club remains fully focused on delivering its objectives both on and off the pitch. We would like to thank our supporters for their continued support."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

FA release statement after video of England team-mates fighting goes viral READ MORE :

Defoe then issued a statement of his own on social media. The 43-year-old explained: "Following recent discussions, I can confirm that I have mutually agreed to leave my position as manager of Woking FC.

‌



"Unfortunately, circumstances have ultimately made it impossible for me to continue in the position. I am extremely proud of the work undertaken during my time at the club and genuinely felt that we were building something special.

"I would like to thank Todd Johnson for giving me the opportunity to manage the club. I am incredibly grateful to the supporters and, most importantly, the players, who I am genuinely gutted for. The group is a fantastic one, and I wish the squad every success for the season ahead.

Which current Premier League star would make the best manager? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Jermain Defoe lasted four months at Woking (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

"I'm really disappointed the journey has ended so soon, but I leave with great pride in what Paul Bracewell, Karl Halabi and I were building at the club.

"My time at Woking FC has been an eye-opening managerial experience and one that will undoubtedly make me stronger for the next challenge in my career."

‌



Defoe took charge of two pre-season friendlies, as Woking faced non-league side Sholing before taking on Portsmouth, one of his former clubs. The Tottenham hero worked as a coach in Spurs' academy for two years before leaving in 2024 to pursue his first head coach role.

That arrived in March with Woking sitting 11th. The Cardinals had sacked Neal Ardley, with ambitions of finishing inside the play-offs. Woking will now look to appoint a new manager in time for the National League season which stars on Saturday, August 8.

Sports.title: Man Utd identify World Cup star as new target after pulling out of Alex Scott transfer
Sports.content:
Man Utd identify World Cup star as new target after pulling out of Alex Scott transfer

Manchester United want to sign a third midfielder before the summer transfer window closes but they've been priced out of a move for Bournemouth star Alex Scott

View 2 Images Danilo played for Brazil at the World Cup (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Manchester United are weighing up a move for ex-Nottingham Forest star Danilo. The news comes after United decided not to pursue a deal for Bournemouth's Alex Scott.

‌



Bournemouth will demand at least £70million for Scott, who was the subject of a £64m bid from Chelsea which was rejected earlier this week. United value the England international at around £40m and will now look at alternative options in their search for a third new central midfielder.

‌



BBC Sport report that the Red Devils have registered their interest in Danilo, who plays for Brazilian side Botafogo. It's added that Newcastle were interested in the 25-year-old earlier this summer.

‌



Danilo made four appearances at the World Cup - all from the bench - as part of Carlo Ancelotti's squad. Botafogo have already received two offers in the region of £25m from Brazilian rivals Palmeiras and Russian heavyweights Zenit St Petersburg.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd given green light for Aurelien Tchouameni transfer as Real Madrid stance emerges READ MORE :

Palmeiras, where Danilo made his name over three seasons, are currently pushing hardest to complete a deal. Botafogo would prefer sell him abroad, having paid £21.7m to sign him from Forest a year ago.

‌



Danilo is one of several options for United, who've also enquired about Real Madrid midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni. The Red Devils have already recruited two midfielders this summer; Andrey Santos for £50m and Youri Tielemans for £35m.

In two-and-a-half years with Forest, Danilo made 62 appearances across all competitions. His third season at the City Ground was blighted by a serious ankle injury which took a toll on him.

Which midfielder should Manchester United sign? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Danilo spent two years at Nottingham Forest before joining Botafogo (Image: Cameron Smith - Danehouse/Getty Images)

"It was really tough at first, but with time it got easier," Danilo told FIFA's website before the World Cup. "I started to understand things differently. I matured a lot.

"I became stronger and learned to think more positively every day. After that injury, I developed this mindset."

Article continues below

Botafogo are having a middling season, sitting 10th in the Brazilian top flight with seven wins, four draws and seven defeats after 18 games. Danilo has been prolific in front of goal, though, scoring seven league goals as well as three in cup competitions.

Sports.title: Man Utd given green light for Aurelien Tchouameni transfer as Real Madrid stance emerges
Sports.content:
Man Utd given green light for Aurelien Tchouameni transfer as Real Madrid stance emerges

Manchester United are interested in signing Aurelien Tchouameni from Real Madrid, lodging an enquiry as they bid to revamp their midfield in the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Aurelien Tchouameni is a target for Manchester United (Image: Stephen Nadler/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Real Madrid are open to selling Aurelien Tchouameni in a major boost to Manchester United's chances of signing him. Tchouameni, 26, has just got back from helping France reach the semi-finals of the World Cup, playing an integral role in Didier Deschamps' side.

‌



But throughout the tournament, his future at club level was a hot topic. United have a long-standing interest in Tchouameni, who Real boss Jose Mourinho initially planned to keep after returning to the Bernabeu this summer.

‌



However, the Sun report that Real are now prepared to let the midfielder go at the right price. The La Liga giants have been linked with a big-money move for Manchester City star Rodri and might need to drum up funds.

‌



United's interest is said to have ramped up since the World Cup ended, with Tchouameni out of contract in 2028. It was reported in Spain earlier this month that Real and the Frenchman had agreed a new five-year deal, although there's been no confirmation.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Manchester United pull out of Alex Scott transfer race after learning asking price READ MORE :

United have already signed two midfielders this summer, paying a combined £85m for Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. But with Manuel Ugarte expected to miss most of the season because of a serious knee injury, the Red Devils want to add a third.

‌



Their search for a specialist defensive midfielder has led them to Tchouameni, whose experience of starting the 2022 World Cup final and winning the Champions League in 2024 appeals to United. The former Monaco star also suits United's preferred age range for signings - between 22 and 26.

How much should Manchester United pay for Aurelien Tchouameni? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Aurelien Tchouameni's contract with Real Madrid expires in 2028 (Image: Marcel Bonte/Soccrates/Getty Images)

‌



Real's pursuit of Rodri could therefore prove to be a double boost for United, as local rivals City would be losing one of their best players. However, Los Blancos could wait until Rodri's contract expires next summer and sign him on a free.

As for Tchouameni, ex-Real midfielder and French compatriot Claude Makelele has warned Bernabeu chiefs not to sell him. Makelele told DAZN: "He was the only player who performed consistently from start to finish.

"Mourinho isn't a fool; he's a good manager, one of the best managers. He knows he's going to need a strong squad to be able to win La Liga."

Sports.title: Arsenal to launch £70m Bruno Guimaraes bid - but transfer for Newcastle star hangs in balance
Sports.content:
Arsenal to launch £70m Bruno Guimaraes bid - but transfer for Newcastle star hangs in balance

Bruno Guimaraes has emerged as a top target for Arsenal this summer in their search for quality reinforcements and they are ready to pay out £70million to sign him

View 2 Images Arsenal want to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle (Image: Getty )

Arsenal are poised to table a £70million bid for Bruno Guimaraes - but will not overpay for the midfielder if Newcastle try to resist a sale.

‌



The Gunners are in the market for quality additions to bolster the squad that won the Premier League and reached the Champions League final last season. And a move for Guimaraes, who boasts extensive top-flight pedigree, appeals in their search for an elite midfielder.

‌



Guimaraes, 28, is known to be keen on the move, which would give him a realistic opportunity to win major trophies.

‌



Newcastle, though, have no appetite to cash in on their talismanic captain — and it remains to be seen if a financial package in the region of £70m would realistically be enough for them to soften that stance.

BBC Sport report that Arsenal are ready to launch an official bid of that amount after stepping up their interest in Guimaraes. However, it's noted that they will not stray from their valuation of the Brazilian.

Whether or not they would consider bidding higher for a player who turns 29 later this year remains to be seen. And if that is the case, then they could opt to move on to other targets.

‌



That stance saw them miss out on a deal for Morgan Rogers, a long-term target who was viewed as the ceiling-raiser signing Arsenal were looking for in their search for a new left-sided attacker.

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes wants to join Arsenal this summer (Image: Getty Images)

The Gunners valued Rogers at £80m; a figure far lower than Aston Villa's valuation of the England star. That gulf in valuations opened the door for Chelsea to swoop in with a £117m offer. Arsenal declined to match it, with Rogers going on to join one of their big domestic rivals.

Article continues below

Rogers' former Aston Villa team-mate, Ezri Konsa, is another player Arsenal are courting with the new Premier League season now just weeks away.

Sports.title: Argentina's shameful behaviour should not let the World Cup's biggest offenders off the hook
Sports.content:
Argentina's shameful behaviour should not let the World Cup's biggest offenders off the hook

Lionel Messi and his beaten Argentina team-mates deserved all the flak that came their way following the World Cup final but that should not give Gianni Infantino and FIFA a reprieve

View 3 Images Lionel Messi has come under fire for his behaviour in the World Cup final (Image: Getty Images)

According to a polling company that might have better things to do, Lionel Messi’s popularity amongst British people has gone down since he tried to get the saintly Marc Cucurella sent off during the World Cup final. It is unclear whether this news is keeping Messi awake at night but you suspect not.

‌



Messi’s lamentable attempt to land Cucurella in trouble was part of a tapestry of unedifying Argentinian antics and was unbecoming of a great player. But it was hardly the crime of the century.

‌



Since when did we become so puritanical? Would Cucurella have done it if the situation of the game had been reversed? Of course he would.

‌



You might hold Messi to a higher moral standard but players trying to get opponents into bother is a staple of the modern game. It did not help Messi’s cause that he was the captain of a squad that turned its back on Spain’s coronation after it had also descended into violent disarray at the final whistle.

Argentina flop's sister makes Falklands Islands claim after World Cup shame READ MORE :

The offending individuals will deserve whatever punishment comes their way and deserved all the criticism that has already come their way. But let’s not pretend we were shocked by the Argentinian reaction to the loss to Spain.

And let’s not allow their behaviour to deflect criticism and scrutiny from where it most needs to be directed most. It needs to be directed most at Gianni Infantino and FIFA.

‌



View 3 Images Bryson DeChambeau threatened to get Donald Trump involved in his rules row at The Open (Image: Richard Heathcote, Getty Images)

When it comes to petulant reactions, there was a belter at Royal Birkdale last Friday after Bryson DeChambeau received a two-shot penalty for what was a debatable rules infringement. It was a slightly controversial decision but one DeChambeau should have taken on the chin.

Instead, he ranted and raved at officials … and, apparently, threatened to call Donald Trump and get him involved. As it happened, the President of the United States never stepped in but you know where the idea came from.

‌



Thankfully, at least one football association is taking a stance. The Norwegians, headed by its federation president Lise Klaveness, are set to make an official complaint to FIFA’s ethics committee over Trump’s involvement in the Folarin Balogun case, which saw the American striker have his red card ban suspended.

View 3 Images Messi has been accused of trying to get Marc Cucurella sent off (Image: AFP or licensors)

Hopefully, more will follow suit. And hopefully, more will tell the relevant committee that the hydration breaks were aberrations that cannot be repeated. Hopefully, more will kick up a serious fuss over ticket prices and already demand changes for the 2030 World Cup.

‌



Never mind the tantrums shown by several Argentinians after the last whistle - and it has to be said that we seem to be more upset by them than the Spanish are - the final itself was a grotesquely gaudy and elongated occasion. Wayne Rooney had it spot on when he said the best thing about the half-time show was when it finished.

Sure, Argentina’s behaviour needs to be punished. And sure, Messi did not cover himself in glory. But the people who really need to be looked at now the World Cup is over are Infantino and FIFA.

Sports.title: Man Utd XI from last Rosenborg friendly with six axed and two more potential transfers
Sports.content:
Man Utd XI from last Rosenborg friendly with six axed and two more potential transfers

A lot has changed since Manchester United last met Rosenborg

View 2 Images Less than half of the starters from Manchester United's previous trip to Rosenborg still play for the club (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United are due to take on Rosenborg this week, some two years on from their last meeting. Those two years have been incredibly eventful, though, with the Premier League club undergoing a huge upheaval - and not just with the playing staff.

‌



Erik ten Hag was still United's manager when that match in Trondheim took place. He had just led the Red Devils to FA Cup glory but pre-season got off to a tough start when Noah Holm scored the winner in Trondheim.

‌



Ten Hag was gone just months later with Ruben Amorim taking his place. However, the Portuguese coach only lasted 14 months in the hotseat before his January 2026 exit, meaning Michael Carrick is in charge for the latest trip to Norway.

‌



Changes in the dugout have also been accompanied by an overhaul of the playing staff. Six of the 11 players who started the last Rosenborg game have since left or retired, while two more could yet leave Old Trafford before the current window is up.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Bruno Fernandes commits future to Manchester United despite new contract wait READ MORE :

Man Utd release new 2026/27 away kit with striking blue design READ MORE :

Radek Vitek started in goal that day and is the sole survivor of the back five still on the books at Old Trafford. The Czech started behind centre-back Jonny Evans - now retired and part of Carrick's coaching staff - and three other defenders now playing elsewhere.

‌



Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Will Fish both left the following month and could end up facing one another in the Championship before too long. Wan-Bissaka's West Ham are newly relegated to the second tier while Fish's Cardiff won promotion last season.

The defence was rounded out by academy graduate Sam Murray, who left for Carlisle in 2025 and is now looking for a new club again. As for Vitek, a promise of first team football could tempt him away.

View 2 Images Aaron Wan-Bissaka left United just a month after the friendly in Norway (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



"At the moment, I am still here, but we will see. I hope so," he said after featuring against Wrexham in United's first friendly of the summer. "I hope there will be some interest. I think you will know when things are more concrete."

Further forward, Casemiro gave United two more years but left in the summer of 2026. The Brazilian is now at Inter Miami, with a strong end to last season not enough to keep him around.

He played in midfield with Mason Mount and Hannibal Mejbri that day. While Mount is still a United player, impressing against Wrexham, Hannibal is long gone.

‌



The Tunisian international sealed a permanent move to Burnley in August 2024 and remains at Turf Moor to this day. He helped the Clarets win promotion to the Premier League but they dropped straight back down last term.

Pre-season regularly gives clubs the opportunity to blood younger talent, particularly while waiting for international players to return from major tournaments. Ethan Williams and Ethan Wheatley are both still at United, having started that Rosenborg game, as are some of the youngsters who came off the bench in Trondheim.

Completing the front three was Marcus Rashford, who had surprisingly been overlooked by Gareth Southgate for England's Euro 2024 squad. The forward spent the 2025/26 season on loan at Barcelona but his future is up in the air again after the Catalan club opted against triggering a buy option, and manager Carrick will have a decision to make on the academy graduate.

Sports.title: Christos Tzolis: How Arsenal's new £34m signing went from Norwich flop to Champions League star
Sports.content:
It says everything about the evolution of Christos Tzolis that Arsenal's newest signing accrued more goal contributions last year than he made league appearances across an ill-fated spell at Norwich City.

The reason Tzolis will play for the newly minted Premier League champions is because, at 24, he is now every inch the clinical, cold-blooded attacker that Europe's elite believed he would become back when he was a teenager. Barcelona were among his illustrious courters back then as heavyweights flocked to observe a prodigious talent. But it was Norwich, rather than Barcelona, who clinched the youngster's sought-after signature.

The Tzolis hype train was already in full flow when the formalities of his £8.8million transfer from PAOK was confirmed back in the summer of 2021. At 21, Tzolis was already a full Greece international; for a Norwich side who were back in the big-time after romping to the Championship title under Daniel Farke, the winger's capture had all the hallmarks of a transfer coup.

And yet, things deteriorated rapidly. After scoring twice in a 6-0 win over Bournemouth in the Carabao Cup on his debut, Tzolis soon fell out of favour. By early November, Tzolis had seen the manager who signed him sacked by the club, just hours after recording Norwich's first league win of the season.

‌



Dean Smith's appointment as Farke's successor proved to be the catalyst for the change of shape which effectively killed Tzolis' Norwich career.

Alex Scott transfer twist as Bournemouth star ‘keen’ on rivals amid Arsenal and Man Utd race READ MORE :

Arsenal respond to Morgan Rogers transfer snub as £34m signing flies in for medical READ MORE :

“It was the hardest year of my career,” Arsenal's newest attacker conceded to Het Nieuwsblad back in 2024. “The first time I didn’t play with the first team, but with the second [reserves], I was very disappointed. That was the lowest point of my career.

“My agent and my family had to convince me not to give up. And life off the pitch wasn’t easy back then.”

In total, Tzolis made just 27 appearances for Norwich before leaving the club permanently in the summer of 2024. The first of two loan spells designed to resurrect his career, with FC Twente, fell flat due to a knee injury. It was in the second tier of German football with Fortuna Dusseldorf that the youngster finally rediscovered his killer instinct, plundering more than 20 goals.

‌



From there, he never looked back. Unsurprisingly, Dusseldorf triggered their option to sign him permanently for just £3m. But it was Tzolis' next move which put the teen prodigy back on the path to superstardom.

Club Brugge swooped in to offer Dusseldorf the chance to effectively double their money instantly. They accepted and, in Belgium, Tzolis has flourished, accumulating more than 20 goals in successive seasons. Not only did he score 22 times last term, he registered a staggering 29 assists to break out as one of the biggest stars in the Belgian Pro League.

View 3 Images Christos Tzolis has transformed into a different player with Club Brugge (Image: JASPER JACOBS, BELGA MAG/AFP via Getty Images)

Tzolis returns to these shores not only hardened by the challenges of his stint in Norfolk, but brimming with confidence. Deadly with his right-foot, he has thrived in a left-sided attacking role and is viewed as the successor to the revered Leandro Trossard, who completed a move to Besiktas last week.

‌



Speaking to The Telegraph, Norwich's sporting director at the time Tzolis was signed, Stuart Webber, cites the physicality of the Premier League as one of the reasons behind the young attacker's failure to live up to expectations. “He was very young, coming into the hardest league in the world where the physicality is off the charts,” said Webber.

“It didn’t work out because we [Norwich] were a struggling team in an unforgiving division. Attacking players don’t get 100 touches of the ball when they are playing for Norwich. If he’d been at an Arsenal he would have probably been successful straight away.”

Tzolis returns to the Premier League a different beast. Naturally, he has grown physically and looks more robust than the twinkle-eyed teenager who was swatted aside both figuratively and literally at Norwich. The numbers he has put up consistently elsewhere in Europe, albeit at a level which is not elite, are eye-catching. His previous experience, although chastening, should give him some form of advantage when it comes to adapting to the rigours of Premier League life this time around.

“I’m a direct player, I go for goals or assists,” Tzolis told Arsenal’s website. “That’s my point of view as an attacker, as a winger. I’m always hungry to score or to give the final pass to my teammates. And I can say I work hard for the team, also in the defensive part.”

‌



View 3 Images Christos Tzolis struggled previously in the Premier League for Norwich City (Image: Ryan Pierse)

Arsenal went into the summer with designs on levelling up their attack, particularly on the left side. A deal for Morgan Rogers is now off the table, and Tzolis will not be the only acquisition in that area. Whereas at Tzolis organically became the main man at Brugge, his role at Arsenal will be significantly different.

There is, of course, the risk that Tzolis' exceptional record in Belgium does not translate to the Premier League. Even with the additional experience and nous under his belt.

In a transfer market where the Premier League's heavyweights have focused on domestic signings for inflated transfer fees this summer, the signing of Tzolis is somewhat of an outlier.

‌



But considering the transfer fee, the prospective upsides to the deal and the fact Arsenal are still after a ceiling-raiser signing for the left wing berth, you can see why signing Tzolis is a risk they feel is worth taking.

Sports.title: 'Good luck to Dirk...': Littler dazzles in Blackpool as 'frightening' form continues
Sports.content:
If a player hit a nine-darter on the World Matchplay stage, that would usually go down as their highlight. That is just the tip of the iceberg for Luke Littler in 2026.

Littler came into Blackpool as the reigning and defending champion with the expectations on his shoulders to deliver.

He has and then some. The numbers are jaw-dropping:

113 average in first round (second-highest at Matchplay behind Phil Taylor's 114.99 in 2010)

109 average in second round and quarter-finals

Nine-darter vs Nathan Aspinall

17 180s vs Josh Rock

14 180s vs Nathan Aspinall

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the quarter-final between Luke Littler and Josh Rock

If his heights were not already incomprehensible, they have gone up a notch.

Not only that, Littler knows he can dominate.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Littler admits he's playing some of the best darts of his career after a dominant win over Rock

"I feel really good up on the stage. Preparations beforehand have gone really well, just relaxing, playing and relaxing again. I am just glad I can perform on the biggest stages," Littler said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the thrilling second-round match between Littler and Nathan Aspinall

"I feel like I can. Obviously a 109 average, a 113 and back down to a 109 average comes with the big finishes. The scoring power is there as well.

"As long as I can keep it up, I'm sure I will dominate. Next game, let's get it back up to the 113s."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Littler produced an incredible nine-darter in the opening leg of his match with Aspinall

That next game will see Dirk van Duijvenbode become the next player charged with attempting to stop Littler in his tracks.

Up to this point, Littler's win over Rock marked the 27th time in a row he won a match that went over 20 legs.

Not only that, Littler continues his quest to become the first player since Michael van Gerwen in 2016 to go back-to-back in Blackpool, and the world No 1 currently holds the World Darts Championship, UK Open, Premier League and Masters. He is also defending the Matchplay, Grand Slam, Grand Prix and the Players Championship Finals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aspinall offers up his darts to the crowd after Littler almost hits his second nine-darter of the match

With all the in mind, Sky Sports Darts' Mark Webster has a simple message for the Dutchman when he takes on the best player in the world on Saturday, live on Sky Sports: "Good luck."

"He can play in spells. I say spells because he's been doing it all tournament. I was delighted for Josh because it was an improved performance and a 101 average but he lost by nine legs so it just shows how good Littler is," Webster said.

"He looks comfortable in every scenario. Good luck to Dirk on Saturday.

"It's 111 tournament average. He's played almost 60 legs. He's just too good! He's focused and relaxed.

"He's by far the best player in the world. It's frightening form."

Image: Littler is producing some stunning stats at the World Matchplay

The quarter-finals continue, live from 7.30pm on Sky Sports Main Event and Action.

Gian van Veen and James Wade will do battle in the quarter-finals for a second year in a row, with the world No 3 looking to avenge his loss to 'The Machine' in 2025.

Then, Gerwyn Price faces Ross Smith. Smith went through to the quarter-finals after Cameron Menzies withdrew from their second-round match in the fourth leg due to illness.

Sports.title: Rovers fight from 12 points behind to claim derby win at Hull FC
Sports.content:
Hull FC 20-34 Hull KR: Rovers fight from 12 points behind to claim Super League derby victory and move back into playoff spots

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hull KR picked up a ninth derby victory over Hull FC in a row, battling from 12-0 behind to win on Thursday Hull KR picked up a ninth derby victory over Hull FC in a row, battling from 12-0 behind to win on Thursday

Defending Super League champions Hull KR moved back into the playoff positions following a 34-20 comeback derby victory at Hull FC from 12 points behind.

Hull FC, who had lost eight derbies in a row heading into this one, started superbly to score twice within the opening eight minutes through Joe Batchelor and Davy Litten for a 12-0 lead.

Yet, Rovers battled back to level by half-time following tries from Tom Amone and Arthur Mourgue.

The Black and Whites briefly led again at 14-12 in the second half via the boot of Zak Hardaker, but a try from Jack Broadbent and penalty from Mourgue soon put the Robins six points ahead.

The match then swung on the next try with 12 minutes to play; Hull FC seemingly ready to score down the right, but Joe Burgess pinching an intercept to race nearly 80 metres down the field for Hull KR's fourth.

Mourgue added another penalty to stretch the lead further, with Jake Arthur's late try for Hull FC academic in the end as Jordan Dezaria forced his way over for another Hull KR effort late in the game.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joe Burgess' lung-busting try made sure of victory for Hull KR Joe Burgess' lung-busting try made sure of victory for Hull KR

Last: We didn't show enough patience - win was in our grasp!

Hull FC coach Andy Last told Sky Sports:

"That was in our grasp. Started the game really well. Got to 12-0. The last 15 minutes of the first half, we started to get a bit of ascendancy in the ruck, but then conceded a couple of soft tries.

"In the second half, we couldn't get out of our half. Hull KR are very good at suffocating field position. We got an opportunity with 15 minutes to go.

"We didn't show enough patience to keep them camped on their end, and the Burgess try was a back-breaker. Got to give credit to Hull KR, they were the better team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hull FC were quick out the blocks as they stunned Hull KR early with two tries inside the first eight minutes Hull FC were quick out the blocks as they stunned Hull KR early with two tries inside the first eight minutes

"We controlled large parts of that game in the first half really well. But the momentum went in the ruck.

"They started to get a little bit of speed, Jez Litten; no surprise he got man of the match. An outstanding player. He dominated large parts of the game for Hull KR, but there's a lesson there for us."

'Proud' Peters: Anyone who questioned our fight - we showed it tonight

Hull KR head coach Willie Peters told Sky Sports:

"That was a relieving victory but naturally, after the start that could have got ugly, but they showed a lot of fight.

"If anyone questioned our fight before the game, that's what I was most proud of. 12-12 at half-time, yeah it wasn't perfect but I wanted to see some fight from the group and they certainly showed that.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hull KR's Tom Amone and Arthur Mourgue score a try each to bring their side back level at half-time Hull KR's Tom Amone and Arthur Mourgue score a try each to bring their side back level at half-time

"You're not calm as a coach during the game. Where we're at as a club, this is all new to us.

"Doing what we did last year, we're in a different position, where teams have hunted us. We find ourselves outside of the six, it's new territory but a great challenge.

"We'll learn a lot about ourselves and the club will at the back end of the year. We want to review it then, not now, we've got a lot of fight left.

"There's no disconnection. When I'm talking about disconnect, it's about things that we do on the field sometimes. One thing I'm strong about is being connected. Connected teams win, simple as that. If we weren't connected, we don't come back to win that game tonight."

Litten: We have a lot to improve on but still the champion team

Player of the match Jez Litten told Sky Sports:

"Always special to play in derbies. It wasn't the prettiest of games but we stuck in there and turned up for each other and I'm happy we got another derby winner.

"It was good the way we did it. We went 12 points behind and showed that resilience. We've had a tough couple of weeks; it only matters to us what we speak about between those four walls of the dressing room.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Hull derby gets heated as both sides are involved in a melee where both FC & KR stars were lucky to avoid punishments for a late challenge and a slap The Hull derby gets heated as both sides are involved in a melee where both FC & KR stars were lucky to avoid punishments for a late challenge and a slap

"We showed that all tonight. We're still the champion team. And we're coming into the business end of the year. Tonight just showed that, we're still the champion team and a lot of teams want to knock us off.

"We're not the full package yet and we have a lot to improve on. We're going to be humble about it and work on our game next week."

Sports.title: Hamilton sends message to title rivals
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says he 'really believes' Ferrari can enable him to fight for an eighth world championship title this season.

Hamilton is second in the standings, 45 points behind Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli going into this weekend's Hungarian Grand Prix - the 11th of the season's 22 currently-scheduled rounds.

It's the first time Hamilton has been in title contention since he was contentiously edged out by Max Verstappen in 2021, and the 41-year-old says he is loving being back in the mix.

"It's amazing," said Hamilton, who has impressed in 2026 following a difficult first campaign with Ferrari.

"It's a great feeling, especially when you look at the contrast of where we were last year here.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Un-named Video

"I'm really proud of the team for the curve and step we have taken collectively and I have to always acknowledge my own efforts and the work I've put in and the changes I've made to enable us to be where we are and I'm really proud of myself for that.

"There's still a lot of work to do and still a mountain to climb ahead of us on the second half of the season but I'm more focused than ever and I really believe we can fight."

Despite Antonelli's superb form, Hamilton is insisting that the Hungarian Grand Prix, the final race before the sport's summer break, is not make or break for his hopes of chasing down the 19-year-old Italian.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton claimed his first win in red at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix

"We are continuing to develop, we are continuing to push," Hamilton said. "There's still a long way to go. I don't see this one or the next one as a break point. I don't know when it becomes the break point, if there is a break point.

"This is just the time for us to continue to hammer down and continue to double down on our development and continue to push.

"We have had two wins as a team, plenty of podiums - we are right there on their (Mercedes') tails and I think we are now able to compete with them more consistently for victories, which I think is positive."

'Mercedes still the car to beat in Hungary'

Ferrari have been touted by some as favourites at the Hungaroring due to an expectation the characteristics of their car will be suited to the circuit.

Ferrari have generally been unable to match the performance of the Mercedes power unit, but the high number of slow corners in Budapest should theoretically make the deficiency less of an issue.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton claims Sprint Pole at the British Grand Prix!

Despite that, Hamilton is taking nothing for granted, and insists Mercedes remain the 'car to beat'.

"I don't want to make assumptions," Hamilton said. "The last couple races, ultimately we should have won the last two races if we perfected the weekend. The car was able to have won.

"In Spa we were more competitive than we thought and I missed something on that weekend and that's not what I want to do this weekend.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive Lewis Hamilton winning a record EIGHTH Hungarian Grand Prix back in 2020

"We have got a car that can compete. I think Mercedes still have the car to beat, naturally, as they have won the most and they won't be easy to beat this weekend.

"But we have made subtle progress and hopefully can fight with them this weekend."

Sports.title: Russell boosted as Mercedes find answer for engine problems
Sports.content:
George Russell is optimistic Mercedes have identified and resolved the glitches that have afflicted his car's power unit ahead of this weekend's Hungarian Grand Prix.

Russell slipped 50 points behind title-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli last weekend at Spa-Francorchamps after making a first-lap exit from the race following contact from Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton.

However, the Briton felt that the race-ending collision, and his difficult weekend relative to an on-form Antonelli as a whole, had been heavily influenced by energy-deployment problems with his engine.

Russell had experienced one straight-line speed glitch over the event's first two days, hurting his car's performance at the end of the long Spa lap, while his race start was hampered by a separate issue which impacted all Mercedes-powered runners and left him vulnerable to cars behind.

But Russell is hopeful Mercedes have managed to get to the bottom of what went wrong and, crucially, managed to fix the issues as F1 prepares for its final race before the summer break in Budapest.

"We're pretty confident we I think we've got on top of the issues that we had in Spa and it should be easy to resolve," he said.

"We hope and we think we have got on top of it, so feeling more positive.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver George Russell spins after contact with Lewis Hamilton and his race ends on the opening lap, but was the Ferrari driver's penalty fair?

"At the time we were not sure what it was but the team have worked so hard to really dig deep.

"I think Spa gave us the right clues where we needed to look and it's only when you look really deep in the right place that you find the problem. Fingers crossed we hope the issue with the power unit has been resolved, but we'll find out this weekend."

Asked to clarify whether the problems had ever been anything to with the way he had been driving the W17, having initially worked through different approaches to tackling the sweeping Belgian lap in practice, Russell said: "We think it was a software bug. It wasn't the driving style that was contributing to the loss of power, so that's something at least.

"I think Spa gave us the right pointers of where to look for the problem. It's like getting a needle out of a haystack really and suddenly when you know where you've got to look maybe the problem you can find and, thankfully, I think we have.

"Time will tell but it wasn't an easy couple of weeks."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player David Croft questions whether George Russell can still win the world championship after he was forced to retire in Belgium, while Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli went on to win the race

'It is the toughest battle psychologically I've had' - Russell opens up on 2026 ups and downs

Russell described his season, in which he started as the clear favourite for the world title, as an "emotional rollercoaster", amid inconsistency in his own form and some costly Mercedes reliability problems.

Asked if it had all contributed to the toughest psychological battle he had faced in his career on track to date, the 28-year-old said: "Yeah, I think it's probably fair to say it is the toughest battle psychologically I've had just because it's been so many ups and downs, combined with things in my control that haven't been great and also with things outside of my control that have hampered the progress and progression.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater discusses the biggest talking points off the back of the Belgian Grand Prix, including if the title chase has been blown for George Russell

"But what doesn't kill you makes you stronger and I sort of feel proud of my resilience and, three days later here after Spa, I feel positive and excited for the weekend and I'm looking at the future prospects and not the past disappointment.

"I guess that's the good thing with racing, you've often got an opportunity just round the corner."

That next opportunity is at the Hungaroring, where Russell has twice finished on the podium and claimed a first career pole position in 2022. The track is not as power dependent as either Silverstone, where Russell said he first experienced the straight-line speed glitch, or Spa.

The Briton is aiming to regain the improved form he believes he had been showing when he won the Austrian Grand Prix three races ago.

"I felt some good momentum coming out of Austria and Barcelona, especially after Monaco," said Russell.

"Monaco was a very low point for me in my season and coming back in Barcelona, getting the pole, the P2 [in the race], getting the pole in Austria and getting the win, I felt a real good momentum building, which was halted in Silverstone and Spa.

"I hope I can continue from where we were in Austria."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch from onboard with George Russell as he crashes out of the Belgian GP after contact with Lewis Hamilton.

He added: I'm just looking forward to coming into Budapest. It's a circuit I like. It's going to be a real challenging weekend.

"We know it's one of the least power-sensitive circuits of the season. We've got Ferrari close behind. They have a better chassis than power unit at the moment, so of all of the circuits, you can expect them to be competitive here.

"Of course, Kimi's performing super well every single race weekend, so it's not going to be a straightforward weekend, but I'm excited for it."

He also insisted that nothing was lost yet in the race for 2026's world title despite Antonelli's increased lead.

"For sure [I can still win it]," added Russell.

"We're not even halfway through yet. It's just been so up and down this whole season. Four races ago I was a lot more points behind in the championship than I am right now even with the disappointments of Spa.

"So I am feeling a lot more positive, excited for the weekend ahead and hopefully now I can just focus on driving quick."

Sports.title: Scheffler bounces back from Open putting woes with strong start in Minnesota
Sports.content:
Scottie Scheffler bounced back from his poor performance with his putter at last week's Open as he returned to PGA Tour action on Thursday to card a six-under par 65 at the 3M Open.

The four-time major champion is three shots off overnight leader Ben Kohles, who wrapped up his round with a sensational eagle on the last to post a score of 62.

Emiliano Grillo, Jackson Koivun and Gary Woodland all sit one shot ahead of Scheffler, tied at seven under par.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jake Knapp just misses out on an ace at the 4th hole during his opening round at the 3M Open

World No 1 Scheffler had a quick turnaround following his tied-fourth finish at Royal Birkdale on Sunday, and began his first round at TPC Twin Cities on the back nine. He started a little slowly by his standards, making a birdie on the 12th hole before adding another on the 18th, despite missing the green with his approach.

From there, he found some momentum, carding a birdie on the first hole despite missing the green, before also making gains on the fourth, sixth and seventh holes.

Despite missing an eagle putt on the sixth and a 15ft birdie putt on the 14th, Scheffler impressed with his flat stick on Thursday afternoon in Minnesota, ranking second in the field for strokes gained putting.

"Fresh greens are a little bit easier than links greens," the world No 1 said. "Part of playing links golf is the ball's not going to roll true every single time.

"I felt like I was just on the wrong end of that last week.

Image: Scheffler ranked second in the field for putting on Thursday afternoon after shooting a six-under par 65

"I got here and made sure I was lined up where I thought it was and made sure I was hitting it on that line and that was about it."

Scheffler added that he would "love to predict" when a good putting day was coming.

"Golf's funny. Some days you're hitting your lines and the line seems to be tracking toward the hole and other days it feels like you're doing the same thing and it kind of goes around the hole.

"But today was a day in which I was able to hole some nice putts and that's why I was able to make some birdies out there."

Elsewhere, England's Jordan Smith returned to the PGA Tour after his impressive tied-18th finish at Royal Birkdale last week.

The 33-year-old got off to a bumpy start, three-putting on the fifth hole for a bogey, cancelling that out with a birdie on the sixth before finding a water hazard with his tee shot on the seventh to go down for a double bogey.

Smith recovered on his back nine to hit birdies on holes 13 and 17 to finish his round at level par.
