Sports.title: Chelsea paid Aston Villa £117m for Morgan Rogers. Is he the right fit?
Sports.content:
It quickly became apparent this summer that Aston Villa would not be holding on to Morgan Rogers. Having helped the club finish fourth in the Premier League and win the Europa League, the 23-year-old was in demand.

Arsenal looked like his likeliest next destination, with the champions eager to strengthen the left side of their attack. The charm offensive came from many angles, with Martin Ødegaard, Mikel Arteta and the club’s England players trying to sell the idea to Rogers. But, with Arsenal reluctant to meet Villa’s asking price, Chelsea intervened and made Rogers the most expensive British player ever, surpassing the £116m that Manchester City paid Nottingham Forest for Elliot Anderson earlier this summer.

Xabi Alonso is new to Chelsea, so it is difficult to know exactly where Rogers will play. The versatile forward, who started out at West Brom before moving to Manchester City, Middlesbrough and then Villa, will probably be used in a variety of roles – often starting from the left but having opportunities to take up various attacking positions.

Alonso predominantly used a 3-4-3 formation at Bayer Leverkusen and a 4-2-3-1 at Real Madrid. If Chelsea play with three at the back, Rogers will be the left-sided No 10 in the team; if they use a four-man defence, he will start slightly wider but with the freedom to come inside – or he might even occupy the central role.

If Alonso goes with the style he used at Leverkusen, Rogers might not be the best fit. During Alonso’s two full seasons in the Bundesliga, the team averaged 62.1% (2023-24) and 59.6% (2024-25) possession. During their title-winning campaign in 2023-24, they went unbeaten all season while dominating the ball and moving up the pitch slowly.

They were set up to patiently build with lots of passes, win back possession quickly if they lost it and keep the ball as close to the opposition’s goal as possible. They made 367 high turnovers, which was 54 more than any other side. This system works best with attacking players who are tidy and intricate in tight spaces. However, Rogers is at his most effective when he can use his pace and gallop into space.

His dribble completion rate last season was 34.2%, which was nothing to shout about. And his completion rate for passes under pressure was 73.4% – again not exceptional. Of the 161 forwards and midfielders who attempted at least 300 passes under pressure last season, Rogers ranked 143rd. The statistics suggest he is not particularly effective in close-quarters engagements.

With space to attack, Rogers is a threat. He made 223 progressive carries last season, the 10th highest among Premier League forwards, wingers and attacking midfielders. Only Cody Gakpo (41) and Matheus Cunha (35) had more carries that ended in shots than Rogers (30). He also created 16 chances for teammates after a carry: only 11 players created more. Rogers’ combined 46 chances created and shots taken following carries put him behind just Jérémy Doku (58), Gakpo (57) and Bukayo Saka (56). Alonso’s passing style may not bring the best from Rogers.

There are reasons for optimism though. Rogers is frequently on the move and that makes him difficult to track. Only four players made more off-ball runs in the league last season; his 160 off-ball runs ending in the box was the eighth highest in the division.

View image in fullscreen A mural of Jude Bellingham and Rogers in Birmingham. Photograph: Christopher Thomond/The Guardian

He also has the potential to form a good relationship with João Pedro. The Brazilian will probably be the focal point of the team and he is not a conventional No 9. He likes to drop deep, link with teammates and be a creator almost as much as a finisher. With Pedro dropping back, there will be room for Rogers to exploit beyond him: he made 258 runs in behind last season, the 12th highest in the league.

Rogers’ strong relationship with Ollie Watkins bodes well for Chelsea. He created 20 open-play chances for Watkins last season, which was the second most from one player to another in the league. Wherever he has played, Rogers has developed an understanding with his teammates. He already has a close friendship with Cole Palmer after their time together in the Manchester City academy.

Rogers’ other great attribute is his ball-striking ability. Since he made his Premier League debut in February 2024, Rogers has scored 21 non-penalty goals from 14.7 non-penalty expected goals. His overperformance of +6.3 is the 10th highest in the league.

Rogers has a great strike on him and it could be a gamechanger for Chelsea, particularly when they play teams employing a low block. His five league goals from outside the box since his Villa debut is bettered by only six players. Few players are as accurate when shooting from distance. It was his shot against Norway that led to Jude Bellingham’s winning goal in the World Cup quarter-final.

Chelsea have paid an incredible amount of money for Rogers and there are reasons to wonder if the move will work tactically. But Rogers has a habit of making an impact regardless of the context. He’s not a right winger but he still made his presence known for England against Argentina in the World Cup semi-final, setting up Anthony Gordon’s opener from the right.

Is he a £117m player? Perhaps not. Will he succeed playing the same way he played at Villa? Perhaps not. But it’s hard to imagine him not making a significant impact at Stamford Bridge.

This is an article by Opta Analyst

Sports.title: From Popp to Diani: 10 women’s transfers you may have missed during the men’s World Cup
Sports.content:
There were a host of big women’s football transfers which were hard to miss across June and July, despite the dominance of the men’s World Cup. Among them were Beth Mead’s move from Arsenal to Manchester City, Mary Earps and Georgia Stanway returning to the Women’s Super League with London City Lionesses and Arsenal, Sam Kerr leaving Chelsea to return to Gotham FC and, most prominently, Alexia Putellas’s game-changing switch from Barcelona to London City.

But here are 10 transfers you might have missed while attention was focused on the action in the US, Canada and Mexico.

Alexandra Popp to Borussia Dortmund

The three-time Champions League winner Alex Popp may be reaching the twilight of her playing career but her move to Borussia Dortmund, signing a three-year contract at the tier-three club, after 14 years with Wolfsburg shows she is not quite ready to hang up her boots. The 35-year-old has been prolific for club and country, scoring 112 goals in 219 games for Wolfsburg and 67 goals in 145 games for Germany prior to her international retirement in 2024. A Borussia Dortmund fan whose “heart beats for this club”, Popp couldn’t pass up the opportunity to assist the development of the women’s team, which was launched in 2020.

Kirsty Hanson to Tottenham

The 28-year-old was a top target for Spurs after a phenomenal fourth season at Aston Villa. Last year Hanson said she was working on adding more goals to her game – come the end of last season she was the third-highest top scorer in the WSL, finishing on 12 in 22 games, which was 43% of Villa’s total tally and only one goal behind second-place Alessia Russo. She heads to a focused Tottenham who are giving their manager, Martin Ho, the tools to push closer to, or even break into, the top four.

Ally Sentnor to Angel City

Sentnor, who was the first overall pick in the 2024 NWSL draft, was the subject of a blockbuster $850,000 (£635,000) trade between Kansas City Current and Angel City on 19 June. She then made her debut for her new side on 3 July, starting a 2-0 win against Orlando Pride. The USA women’s national team player has scored seven goals and provided three assists in 23 international games and, at just 22 years old, has a lot of football ahead of her.

View image in fullscreen Ally Sentnor (right) on the ball for Angel City in a 2-0 win against against Chicago Stars last weekend. Photograph: Shaina Benhiyoun/SPP/Shutterstock

Felicia Schröder to Real Madrid

Many clubs were circling but in the end Felicia Schröder completed a big-money move from Häcken to Real Madrid. Multiple Swedish outlets reported the deal for the 19-year-old forward was worth over 15m Swedish kronor (£1.15m). She attracted attention from across the world as she racked up 91 goals in 128 games for Häcken and starred in Uefa’s inaugural women’s Europa Cup competition, finishing as top scorer with eight goals, four of which came in the two-legged final against Hammarby.

Manaka Matsukubo to Chelsea

The versatile 21-year-old, who can play as a forward or attacking midfielder, joined Chelsea from North Carolina Courage for an undisclosed fee but, as one of the most exciting young talents in the women’s game, it’s unlikely she came cheap. The Japan international scored 11 goals, became the youngest NWSL player to score a hat-trick, and was named NWSL midfielder of the year in 2025. She was up to five goals in nine games in the 2026 season before Chelsea swooped earlier this month.

View image in fullscreen Manaka Matsukubo at her Chelsea unveiling. Photograph: Harriet Lander/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Johanna Rytting Kaneryd to OL Lyonnes

The 29-year-old won three league titles, two FA Cups and two League Cups with Chelsea, including a domestic treble in . Rytting Kaneryd is one of several attacking players to leave Chelsea this summer with Sam Kerr, Guro Reiten and Catarina Macario also having departed as they revamp their front line in an effort to reclaim their WSL crown after Manchester City ended their six-year title-winning run.

Noémie Mouchon to Everton

The loss of the forward Kelly Gago, who has signed for West Ham, has been tempered a little by the arrival of the French striker Noémie Mouchon from Leicester. Mouchon did not have the easiest time at Leicester after arriving from Reims with expectations high. The 23-year-old sustained an anterior cruciate ligament injury one month into her first season in the WSL and was ruled out for the remainder of the campaign. She made 16 appearances and scored two goals in the WSL last season but made only two starts. Everton will be hoping she can find the form that helped her to nine goals in 22 games for Reims in the 2023-24 season.

Denise O’Sullivan to Gotham (on loan)

The influential Republic of Ireland midfielder returns to the NWSL with Gotham after six months with Liverpool. The 32-year-old spent 10 seasons in the US before her January move to Liverpool, with Houston Dash and North Carolina Courage (albeit with a number of loan spells in Australia and England). She won the NWSL Shield in 2017 and again in 2018 and 2019 when Courage also secured the NWSL Championship, with O’Sullivan named the side’s MVP in both years. She has 22 goals in 132 games for Ireland.

View image in fullscreen Denise O’Sullivan (right) showing off her close control against Aston Villa last season. Photograph: Nick Taylor/Liverpool FC/Getty Images

Bethany England to Crystal Palace

Bethany England’s Tottenham departure was mourned by fans, with the former Chelsea forward having become the team’s record goalscorer in the WSL with 32 in three-and-a-half seasons, helping them to a first FA Cup final in 2024. The 32-year-old has signed a two-year contract with Crystal Palace, who earned promotion back into the top flight with a second-place finish in WSL2. After four WSL titles, two FA Cups and two League Cups with Chelsea, England brings a wealth of experience to Palace.

Kadidiatou Diani to London City Lionesses

The arrival of Alexia Putellas and Mary Earps has dominated the London City Lionesses transfer talk, while the acquisition of the France forward Kadidiatou Diani from Lyonnes for more than £500,000 has flown somewhat under the radar. The 31-year-old scored 41 goals in 93 games in three seasons for the Champions League giants following her stunning 92 goals in 168 games for Paris Saint-Germain. Michelle Kang, who owns both London City and Lyonnes, will be hoping she brings that edge up front to the ambitious WSL side. They finished sixth last season, their debut campaign in the top flight, nine points behind Tottenham, but they want more and are spending big to make progress.

Sports.title: Elliot Anderson lauds City as ‘kings of Manchester’ after £116m Forest transfer
Sports.content:
Elliot Anderson has called Manchester City the “kings of Manchester” after completing his £116m move to the club from Nottingham Forest.

The 23-year-old was a key part of England’s third-place finish at the World Cup, having been an ever-present for Forest in the Premier League last season. Before Morgan Rogers’ £117m transfer to Chelsea from Aston Villa on Tuesday, Anderson’s fee was the record for a British player.

The midfielder is taking a three-week break after his exploits in North America but is clearly relishing the prospect of playing for City, picking out the first Manchester derby of the new season on 13 September as a standout fixture. He may well be in line for a hot reception from the Old Trafford faithful given his claims about City’s superior status.

“It’s one of the biggest derbies in the world and for as long as I’ve known Manchester, City have been the kings of Manchester,” Anderson said in an interview on City’s website. “It’ll be a great fixture and I can’t wait to be involved in something like that.

“They’re winners, they’re relentless, and that’s the sort of team I want to be a part of – champions and people who win trophies,” Anderson said of his reason for signing for City.

“Over the last 10, 12 years, they’ve dominated, so that’s why I wanted to join. It’s happened quite quick, but I think I always believed I could get to this point and this is where I want to be. Now that I’m here, I’ll keep pushing and try to take this club forward.” Anderson’s rise has been rapid, with his England debut coming as recently as last September, in a 2-0 victory over Andorra.

The Tyneside-born player, who began his career at Newcastle before joining Forest for £35m in July 2024, believes there is much more to come. “I’m only 23, so I’ve got plenty of time to get to my best levels and I definitely think I’m not there yet,” he said.

The deal was agreed three weeks ago but finalised this week after the player’s return from the World Cup. Anderson has signed until 2031 and is City’s first major signing since Enzo Maresca succeeded Pep Guardiola as manager. He is looking forward to working with the Italian. “I’ve watched his teams over the past couple of years and spoke to a few of the lads from Chelsea and they all rate him very highly,” Anderson said.

“I like to be intense when I play and use lots of energy around the pitch and get the fans going. So, I think that’ll be good.”

Kevin De Bruyne, who departed City two summers ago, is an idol for Anderson. “Growing up through the academy at Newcastle, I’ve always wanted to play like him,” Anderson said. “I’ve watched him all the time and to be sat here in the team that he was doing it for is so special.”

Anderson led the Premier League last season in most touches (3,300), most duels won (297) and winning possession (306). “I think I bring a bit of everything. I bring quality, physicality, energy,” he said. “I’d like to think I’d get them [the City supporters] excited, get them off their feet and bring energy to the team.”

Anderson spent half a season on loan at Bristol Rovers in 2022 and became known as the “Geordie Maradona” among supporters. “They started that and it sort of stuck everywhere I’ve been,” he said. “It makes me happy and it gives me real confidence.”

Reflecting on the World Cup, Anderson added: “It was disappointing, but I loved it personally. We had the whole country behind us and we’ve done so well but just fell short. From a personal point of view, I thought I did pretty well.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa seal loan signing of Alejandro Garnacho from Chelsea
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have confirmed the loan signing of the Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho, as a summer of change continues at Villa Park.

The deal for Garnacho’s season-long loan includes a conditional obligation to buy a player who joined Chelsea last August from Manchester United in a deal worth £40m. Villa will be expected to pay a similar fee for Garnacho, who struggled to impress at Stamford Bridge despite featuring in 43 games in all competitions and scoring eight goals.

Garnacho has been allowed to depart Stamford Bridge after being informed he was not guaranteed regular playing time under the club’s new manager, Xabi Alonso. He did not report for duty when Chelsea players returned for pre-season, as pre-arranged.

It was agreed he would stay away from the training ground while any departure was finalised. Named in Argentina’s initial 55-man selection, he missed out on this summer’s World Cup.

“We are delighted with Alejandro. He is so talented, young and he ⁠showed us his wish to help our ​project. We are ‌really happy,” ‌Unai Emery said.

Villa’s third signing of the summer, to follow the arrivals of Johan Manzambi and João Gomes, comes via a familiar trade route. The £117m deal that took Morgan Rogers to Stamford Bridge earlier this week continued a run of transfers between the two clubs, incorporating Carney Chukwuemeka’s and Omari Kellyman’s sale to Chelsea in 2022 and 2024, Ian Maatsen heading in the reverse direction in 2024 and Axel Disasi’s brief 2025 loan to Villa.

Another former Chelsea charge, Jadon Sancho, spent last season on loan at Villa from United and, despite becoming a free agent, he was not signed. Youri Tielemans has also departed Villa for Manchester United this month after his £35m release clause was triggered as the Europa League champions rebuild as a Champions League club, though one under Uefa sanction.

Earlier this summer Villa received a partially suspended £19.4m fine by Uefa for a “significant breach” of squad-cost rule for 2025. Depending on the club significantly decreasing their squad-cost ratio in 2026, £12.9m is suspended, with the club restricted on the registration of new players on their squad list for the coming Champions League season.

Sports.title: ‘Don’t become the protagonist’: Andoni Iraola on the secret of Spain’s success and his role at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Over coffee in Liverpool’s plush hotel in Chicago, Andoni Iraola presents his theory for the phenomenal success of Basque and Spanish coaches. It is a theory that will shape his entire approach to life as the Liverpool head coach and his attempts to bring the connection, the joy and the belief back to Anfield. It centres on the power of the collective.

The Champions League, the Premier League, the Europa League, the FA Cup, the League Cup, the European Championship and, as of Sunday, the World Cup: all currently in the hands of Basque and Spanish coaches, even if Pep Guardiola has since taken his leave from Manchester City. Next season, four men from the small Basque region of Gipuzkoa will manage four of the Premier League’s main contenders, Iraola included, alongside Mikel Arteta, Xabi Alonso and Unai Emery. There is, Iraola believes, a simple explanation for the rise of the guys from Gipuzkoa and for Spanish dominance across a global stage.

“They ask me why a lot of Basque managers especially have arrived to this level and why Spanish teams are winning a lot of things,” Iraola explains. “I always say that a sense of collectiveness is very important. Spain has never had the best athletes. If you analyse in swimming, boxing, track and field, Spain don’t normally win medals. But in collective sports they are very good. In football, basketball, handball, hockey, normally they have good teams. We always put the team first. An example is someone like Rodri. He didn’t score or make an assist but at the end they won the World Cup and he won best player of the tournament. Team-first was always integrated in how we were raised.”

Iraola, warm and friendly despite the jetlag at the start of Liverpool’s pre-season tour of the US, then gives an immediate example of how he embodies those values. He is asked about a letter he sent to Liverpool in January 2014 when, as captain of boyhood club Athletic Club, he rejected the opportunity to sign for Brendan Rodgers’s team. By all accounts courteous and apologetic, as well as highly unusual, the letter provides a telling insight into Iraola’s character. It is an open goal of a question to a new head coach wanting to win over a new fanbase. But Iraola declines to shoot.

Following a lengthy pause, he says: “I don’t know if I want to tell this story so early in my career here. I would like to win some games first. It is a nice story but if you remember me in some months, then you can ask me again. I don’t like to do this from the beginning. I just don’t want to. It will look like I am selling myself. We need some time, and to win some games.”

Iraola’s outlook is refreshing – “Don’t become the protagonist,” he says of his role – and one that Liverpool can easily identify with. Continuing with the theme of Spain’s collectiveness, he adds: “I think there has to be something in society. It cannot only just be about football. I think things work when we are not just selfish, no? When, in the end, you prioritise the situation of the one who has less. That happens also in football. The ones that don’t play, the ones who come from the academy, the ones who earn less. You can compare it with society.”

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola will hope to inspire Jeremie Frimpong this season after his disappointing debut campaign at Anfield. Photograph: Nick Taylor/Liverpool FC/Getty Images

But, and it is a “but” that needs saying given what Iraola hopes to achieve, there were few signs of togetherness at Liverpool last season as Arne Slot’s reign unravelled amid acrimony in the dressing room and in the crowd. The power of the individual took over, and the power of the team appeared secondary. Mohamed Salah’s frequent attempts to undermine his former, title-winning coach was not the only example of that last season.

“I cannot change the personality of the players,” says Iraola, who will manage for the first time as Liverpool head coach on Saturday against Sunderland in Nashville. “Some players are very different to me but they are great players. I don’t want to change everyone and what they think is the best way. But I think we need to think collectively in this game. As a player you are always selfish. You always want to play, you always want to get your stats, you always want to play all the minutes, but I think there has to be an understanding that this is not going to always happen and still I have to be helpful with my teammates and with the team.

double quotation mark I always say we are assistants to the players. They are the main part Andoni Iraola

“The first thing we have to do is try to play well, but it’s not just only about playing well. Supporters have to identify with what they see on the pitch. Sometimes it’s not about just putting one ball in the top corner. A lot of the time, the ones watching the game, OK, they cannot do that but they can run, they can fight for the balls, they can press, they can fight until the last line for every situation and when they see this from the players of their team it’s easier to get behind that team. I will encourage my team to give them these things.”

Iraola never came close to signing for Liverpool 12 years ago despite the best efforts of Michael Edwards, until recently the chief executive of football for the club’s owners, Fenway Sports Group. “I never really wanted to leave Athletic Club,” their former right-back admits. “For me, Athletic Club was the place to be. The only way of leaving was to go to the MLS [with New York City FC] and try something completely different. I didn’t want to become a problem for the club.”

The 44-year-old, however, does see parallels between his boyhood club and his new one. He explains: “This is one of the biggest clubs in the world and, in some way, the comparison to Athletic Club probably isn’t fair, but in a lot of ways I see a lot of similar things. This sense of belonging, of being a little bit different. This connection, also, with players from the academy. The atmosphere of Anfield.”

At his official unveiling in Liverpool last week, Iraola said he intends to immerse himself in the city and “take some pictures” of the tourist spots. The truth is he has already done so. He visited the city a few times during his playing days with Athletic and for a very simple reason. “It had the best flight connections,” he laughs. “The best connections were Manchester and Brussels and sometimes we only had two or three days so the main thing was to go somewhere quick. I remember the first time I went to Liverpool it was already the Christmas market so it was probably around the November international break. We had no kids at the time so we are talking about a lot of years ago but it was a lovely time with my wife.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There has been no holiday this summer for Iraola and his family, now extended by two children. “I went home for one week in the half-term for the kids at the end of May,” he says. “That was once the season had ended. I have mostly been in Bournemouth but I also had some trips to Liverpool to sort the schools and the housing. This is the stuff I wanted to do before I started working officially.”

Iraola describes the process of leaving Bournemouth after three impressive years as “very, very clean” and claims he only started considering his next step once last season had ended with the club in Europe for the first time. The process of becoming Slot’s replacement “was actually quite fast”. He says: “Honestly. It was true that I was talking with some clubs [Milan, Bayer Leverkusen and Crystal Palace all made approaches]. I think it was the first or second week after the season ended. But it happened fast. They contacted me, and it didn’t take a lot [to say yes to Liverpool this time].”

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola answers questions in the US before Liverpool’s opening pre-season game against Sunderland on Saturday. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

It hasn’t taken long for Liverpool fans to create a song in honour of their new head coach. Sung to the tune of Christy Moore’s Viva la Quinta Brigada, written about Irish volunteers who fought against Franco’s fascist forces in the Spanish civil war, the song went viral within days of Iraola’s appointment in June. He is genuinely astonished when told, almost spluttering over a second cup of coffee.

“A new one?” Iraola asks incredulously. “For me it is a strange situation because I always understand that football is about the players. At the beginning when I arrived in England, I remember the first few games I didn’t go with the players to clap the supporters after games. Tommy and Shaun [Elphick and Cooper, Bournemouth assistants who have followed Iraola to Liverpool] said I should join in. In Spain, normally you leave it to the players; they are the ones who have played the game and we are the ones who stayed behind. In England, managers are the ones who go to the fans, so I have done it every time.

Quick Guide Liverpool and Newcastle plan Keegan tributes Show Newcastle and Liverpool are in discussions over a tribute to Kevin Keegan before the clubs meet for their opening fixture of the new Premier League season at St James' Park on 23 August. Keegan rose to prominence at Liverpool, later becoming a folk hero on the pitch and as manager on Tyneside. The former England striker's death at the age of 75 was announced on Monday, and Newcastle have confirmed that both clubs are talking about a shared tribute. 'The opening Premier League match of 2026-27 sees Newcastle United hosting Liverpool – where Kevin made 323 appearances between 1971 and 1977,' a statement on the club website said. 'To ensure his memory is marked fittingly before the game, the club is in communication with Liverpool and will work closely with supporter groups ... and the Premier League, to shape tributes.' Newcastle will hold a minute's silence before their friendly at Gateshead on Saturday, while during their trip to Bristol City, Keegan’s image will be shown on the stadium’s screens in the seventh minute, a reference to the shirt number he wore during his distinguished career. In addition, the club will consult Keegan’s family 'at the appropriate time' as they consider options for a permanent memorial. PA Media Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“These are the cultural things you have to learn when you arrive in a new league. But I always say we are assistants to the players. They are the main part. Our main thing is to help them and they are the only ones who can give us success. We are not as important as they are, that is pretty clear.”

The Kop may dispute that theory, but not Iraola’s take on the power of the collective if restored to full working order.

Sports.title: Norway considers filing Fifa ethics complaint over Trump role in World Cup red card saga
Sports.content:
Donald Trump’s role in clearing Folarin Balogun from a mandatory one-game ban at the World Cup is set to provoke a formal complaint to Fifa ethics investigators.

The Norway soccer federation said Thursday its board of directors will consider filing the complaint at its next meeting, likely on 6 August.

“We need our leader in Fifa to say that this was an error,” Norwegian federation president Lise Klaveness told the Times in an interview published Thursday.

After Trump called Fifa president Gianni Infantino, a one-game ban for Balogun’s red-card tackle against Bosnia and Herzegovina was deferred so he could play against Belgium with a quarterfinals place at stake.

Belgium beat the US 4-1 after a chaotic 36 hours at the World Cup. The Belgium players were seemingly fired up by one of the all-time controversies in tournament history.

Trump called the referee’s red card for Balogun after video review a “horrible” call and took credit for getting Fifa to review what should routinely have been a one-game ban.

“We all know that this verdict was influenced from external forces and did not have the proper process,” Klaveness told the Times of the Fifa ruling that was unprecedented in the past 60 years at World Cups. “When you bend a rule like this, you’re on a slippery slope that will put the whole game at risk,” said the former Women’s World Cup player for Norway, who is an elected member of European soccer body Uefa’s executive committee.

Klaveness is a lawyer and judge who has positioned the Norwegian federation as a conscience in world soccer since her election in 2022. “It is a worry for the game when you compromise fundamental rules of the game,” she said Thursday about not enforcing Balogun’s ban.

Norway previously joined a London-based NGO’s complaint to the Fifa ethics committee alleging Infantino breached a statutory duty of political neutrality, including by creating a peace prize to award to Trump at the World Cup draw in December.

The close personal and political ties between Trump and Infantino include the US president believing the soccer official could be a good pick as next secretary general of the United Nations, the New York Post reported this week.

The human rights NGO, FairSquare, also has filed an ethics complaint about the Balogun incident to the International Olympic Committee, where Infantino is an elected member, about breaching its rules on political neutrality.

Fifa and the IOC rarely acknowledge or provide updates on potential cases before their ethics bodies. The independence of Fifa’s process to handle complaints alleging unethical conduct has been questioned since the lead investigator and judge both were replaced in 2017, in the second year of Infantino’s presidency. Fifa has yet to publish documents explaining how its disciplinary judges reached verdicts about Balogun or other World Cup players.

Sports.title: Police call on English football clubs to ease security burden on taxpayers
Sports.content:
The number of football matches in England and Wales featuring incidents reported to police reached record levels last season, even as the number of arrests continued to return to pre-Covid figures.

According to an annual report by the Home Office, released on Thursday, there was a 4% increase in the number of matches with reports of “football-related anti-social behaviour, violence and disorder” during the 2025-26 season. Reports were made at 1,644 games, up from 1,580 the previous campaign.

Meanwhile, the Home Office calculated there were four arrests (or other actions such as voluntary police interviews) for every 100,000 people attending a men’s football match in 2025-26, with the FA Cup the most likely competition for arrests to be made. Across the women’s game, however, that number falls to four in total.

Quick Guide How do I 

The total number of arrests last season stood at 1,695, down from 1,744 in 2024-25 and a peak of 2,198 during the pandemic-affected campaign of 2021-22. Contained within these figures was an increase in the number of arrests and other actions related to public disorder, the most common type of offence.

This year’s figures in part reflect a change in the data being collected. Last season, for example, the crime of “unauthorised entry” was added to the Football Spectators Act 1989. There were 45 arrests made under the new law in 2025-26, meaning total arrests and actions would otherwise have declined by 4%.

New categories of “sexism and misogyny” and “violence against women and girls” were also added to the list of behaviours that can be reported by supporters, either to police or to bodies such as the FA or Kick It Out. The Home Office said 22 matches were reported for instances of sexist behaviour and 37 for violence against women. “The overall increase was therefore largely driven by the introduction of these new categories”, a Home Office statement said.

Of the incidents reported, the most common type was “hate crime”, which was reported at 491 matches. The second most common was reports of missiles being thrown (359 games) and then the use of pyrotechnics (316 matches).

In other data released by the Home Office, the number of football banning orders – a sanction that prevents someone convicted of a football-related crime from attending matches – issued was at its highest level since 2012. Currently there are 2,460 FBOs in place. This is up by 568 on the previous season, but a smaller rise than the 685 recorded in 2024-25.

Chief constable Mark Roberts, the lead for football policing in England and Wales, said the latest Home Office report showed the need to revisit the funding of football policing, with 46% of arrests and actions taking place outside of stadiums. “Football-related crime doesn’t simply stop when fans exit the stadium, but under the current system multibillion-pound football clubs do not have to pay a penny towards the policing outside their grounds,” Roberts said. “This means that taxpayers are left footing the £70m bill each season, which simply cannot continue.”

A Premier League spokesperson said: “The Premier League and its clubs work closely with police forces at a national and local level to ensure safe and welcoming environments for all fans. We are investing more than £90m a season in stewarding, security, crime prevention in communities and a series of technology-led pilots in partnership with a number of police forces and the UKFPU (United Kingdom Football Policing Unit).

“This partnership approach will help the police to safely reduce the demand for policing around football matches, as the number of arrests continue to fall significantly over the last decade.”

Sports.title: Arsenal sign Greece forward Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge for £34m
Sports.content:
Arsenal have completed the £34m signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge. The Greece international, 24, has signed a five-year contract with the Premier League champions and arrives as a replacement for Leandro Trossard following the Belgian’s switch to Besiktas.

Tzolis’s move to the Emirates Stadium – Arsenal’s third permanent transfer of the summer – arrives 48 hours after the north Londoners missed out on Morgan Rogers who signed a £117m British-record fee with Chelsea, describing his new employers as the “biggest club in London”.

Tzolis scored 43 times in 108 appearances for Club Brugge, and lined up in the Belgians’ 3-0 Champions League defeat by Mikel Arteta’s side in December. “I need some time to realise it, I think,” Tzolis said. “⁠It’s absolutely amazing to sign for such a big ​club, the champions of ‌England. I’m very ‌proud to be part of this team for ‌the next season.”

Arsenal’s sporting director Andrea Berta added: “We’re delighted to have completed the signing of Christos. [He] is an extremely versatile attacking player who naturally operates on the left but is comfortable across the front line. He’s an excellent finisher with both feet, thrives in tight spaces, and possesses incredible technical ability.

“Christos has produced outstanding numbers in terms of goals and assists over the last three seasons, and he’s a player who will raise the technical level of our squad, while bringing positive energy, enthusiasm and a strong mentality to our team. We’re confident Christos will make a significant contribution to our club, and we hope our supporters will enjoy watching him play in an Arsenal shirt. We look forward to sharing this exciting new chapter together.”

Tzolis played 14 Premier League games for Norwich during the 2021-22 campaign but his only two goals at the club came in the League Cup. Loan periods with Twente and Fortuna Düsseldorf followed before he made the move to Brugge in 2024.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Greek follows Piero Hincapié – who turned his temporary deal with Arsenal into a full-time switch – and goalkeeper Illan Meslier, a free signing from Leeds, as the Gunners’ third signing. The announcement arrives as a welcome boost for Arteta after defender William Saliba was this week ruled out for an “extensive period” with the back problem the curtailed his World Cup. The France international is set to miss the start of Arsenal’s Premier League defence.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua refuses to talk about Tyson Fury clash ahead of comeback fight against Kristian Prenga - with bout versus the Gypsy King on the cards if both stars win this weekend
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua refuses to talk about Tyson Fury clash ahead of comeback fight against Kristian Prenga - with bout versus the Gypsy King on the cards if both stars win this weekend

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Anthony Joshua shut down talk of Tyson Fury and insisted there is 'no future' beyond Saturday night unless he first gets the job done against Kristian Prenga in Jeddah.

The long-awaited Battle of Britain showdown with Fury is edging ever closer, with both heavyweights taking interim bouts this weekend before an expected blockbuster collision later this year.

Fury boxes Mariusz Wach in Thailand on Friday before Joshua makes his return against the heavy-hitting Albanian less than 24 hours later.

But despite the frenzy surrounding what could finally become one of British boxing's biggest-ever fights, Joshua made it clear he has no interest in looking past the man standing across the ring from him.

'Look, respect my opponent here,' Joshua said when questions during Thursday's press conference turned towards Fury.

'We don't want to talk about Tyson Fury. Respectfully, I have done all the media that I can about what the future holds but you know our focus is him and his team.

Anthony Joshua (left) is refusing to entertain talk of a clash with Tyson Fury ahead of his comeback fight

'We have been working since January, working hard, keeping my head down, aligned all my stars and I am fully focused.'

Joshua acknowledged the excitement surrounding what could await him if he comes through unscathed, but stressed that those conversations count for nothing unless he delivers in Saudi Arabia.

'I understand there is a big picture. The goal is to conquer the universe, right? But first we must conquer earth. My target is here.'

It is a mindset forged by the toughest period of his life.

Saturday marks Joshua's first appearance since stopping Jake Paul in Miami last December, just days before tragedy struck when close friends Latif 'Latz' Ayodele and Sina Ghami were killed in a car accident in Nigeria.

The devastating loss forced Joshua away from boxing as he grieved, with serious doubts over whether he would ever fight again.

Instead, he eventually returned to training and rebuilt towards what could become the defining final chapter of his career.

Victory over Prenga is expected to pave the way for the fight fans have demanded for more than a decade, but Joshua insists he cannot afford to think beyond the immediate task.

Fury (pictured) and Joshua are expected to clash this year but must first both win this weekend

'When you speak to me about what may lay ahead or I sit down in an office with Eddie (Hearn) and he presents to me what may lay ahead, it is a great opportunity for me to understand where this checkpoint takes me and what it leads me on to,' Joshua said.

'The reality of the matter is there is no universe, there is no future unless I get past this checkpoint on Saturday night.'

Prenga arrives in Jeddah with 20 knockouts to his name, although the Albanian has never shared the ring with an opponent anywhere near Joshua's calibre.

For the 35-year-old, however, Saturday represents the opportunity he has spent a lifetime chasing.

'I work all my life for this, I waited all my life for this and I hope I am going to show the world on Saturday who I am,' Prenga said.

Sports.title: Shocking moment Bryson DeChambeau's wayward drive nearly hits a fuming Ian Poulter on the head
Sports.content:
Shocking moment Bryson DeChambeau's wayward drive nearly hits a fuming Ian Poulter on the head

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Ian Poulter narrowly avoided disaster at LIV Golf UK on Thursday as a loose drive from Bryson DeChambeau nearly hit him in the head.

Veteran Poulter, 50, was left livid with his rival as he prepared to take his own shot on the fairway, but no 'fore' shout came from the American.

DeChambeau watched on as the Englishman turned around, raging, after the ball had landed around a metre from him.

Poulter gave a sarcastic shout of 'fore' in the direction of DeChambeau, after the crowd had reacted in shock after the Englishman narrowly avoided a nasty injury.

The ironic shout from Poulter was in reference to the shout golfers usually make when a ball is set to land near an opponent.

DeChambeau opted to slap his thigh in frustration at the JCB Golf and Country Club in Rocester.

A CRAZY moment in #LIVGolfUK as Ian Poulter is nearly hit by a Bryson DeChambeau tee-off 😱



📺 Watch LIV Golf live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/EywP5y88eu — TNT Sports (@tntsports) July 23, 2026

Bryson DeChambeau nearly hit Ian Poulter in the head with a wayward drive at LIV Golf

It had appeared, though, that no one told him his effort was heading for an opponent, and a calmer Poulter had that view when speaking about it after the day's play.

Sports.title: Katarina Johnson-Thompson and Dina Asher-Smith among NINE English call-offs in major blow for Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games
Sports.content:
The Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games suffered a major blow ahead of last night’s opening ceremony when nine English athletes pulled out on the eve of the event.

Heptathlete Katarina Johnson-Thompson and sprint star Dina Asher-Smith were the two leading lights to withdraw and they were joined by fellow Olympic medallists Matthew Hudson-Smith and Daryll Neita as well as 400m runner Amber Anning.

Hammer thrower Anna Purchase, middle distance runner Elliot Giles and sprinter Jona Efoloko also pulled out alongside steeplechaser Zac Seddon.

The loss of Olympic silver medallists Johnson-Thompson and Asher-Smith represents a significant blow to the competition’s organisers, with the former having been expected to target a hat-trick of Commonwealth Games titles having previously won gold in both Gold Coast and Birmingham.

Instead, she has chosen to prioritise the European Championships which are set to take place in Birmingham next month.

Johnson-Thompson has prioritised the upcoming European Championships in Birmingham

‘I’m gutted to have to pull out of this year’s Commonwealth Games,’ said Johnson-Thompson. ‘I was so looking forward to competing on home soil and having the chance to defend my Commonwealth title.

‘Although the injury I picked up earlier this season has improved, I haven’t been able to get back to the level I need to compete at my best.

‘After discussing it with my team, we’ve made the difficult decision to focus on giving myself the best chance of being ready for the European Championships. So I’m working very hard to be there later this season.

‘Missing a championship is never easy but I know it’s the right decision.’

The hectic schedule has presented a quandary for a number of leading athletes, including Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson, who decided not to pursue selection for the Glasgow Games.

Asher-Smith would have been one of the main draws in the women's relay event in Glasgow

International stars who have previously pulled out of the Games include multiple Olympic swimming medallists Kaylee McKeown and Summer McIntosh of Australia and Canada respectively, Hodgkinson’s 800m rival, Mary Moraa of Kenya, and St Lucia’s 100m Olympic champion Julien Alfred.

Away from the athletics track, triple Olympic gymnastics champion Max Whitlock was forced to call time on his comeback bid earlier this month due to injury.

These Games were supposed to be hosted by Australia in March, but the Victorian state pulled out due to budgetary pressure and Glasgow stepped in at late notice.

Sports.title: Chelsea close in on £55m agreement for Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix as Arsenal announce £34m signing of Christos Tzolis: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Fulham keeping an eye on young Real Madrid talent

Fulham have asked to be kept informed on a number of Real Madrid players, as has been widely reported, but among them is Thiago Pitarch.

At 18 years and 226 days, Pitarch became the club's youngest player to start twice in the Champions League knockout stages, surpassing Brazil forward Vinicius Jr's record by 10 days.

He impressed in Madrid's 3-0 win over Manchester City in March and has arrived back in training determined to impress Jose Mourinho and fight for a first team place.

Fulham have asked to be kept informed on a number of Real Madrid players, among them Thiago Pitarch

However, Alvaro Arbeloa is hoping that Mourinho decides a loan and season in the Premier League could prove more beneficial to his development. Fulham do face competition from other Spanish sides too.

Chelsea close in on £55m Maxence Lacroix

Chelsea are closing on agreement over a deal for Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix worth around £55m.

As Daily Mail Sport reported on Monday, talks accelerated over a meeting in New York at the weekend.

Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali and Palace chairman Steve Parish, who were in New York for the World Cup final, met at the Aman Hotel near Central Park on Sunday.

Chelsea are closing on agreement over a deal for Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix

Daily Mail Sport revealed Chelsea had revisited their interest in the 26-year-old early this summer.

The France international cost Palace £18m from Wolfsburg but has been an outstanding performer in the Premier League and Europe.

Crystal Palace locked in Matsima talks

Crystal Palace are continuing talks to sign centre-back Chrislain Matsima from Augsburg.

As negotiations carry on with Chelsea over the structure of a fee on the sale of Maxence Lacroix, Palace are looking to bolster their defensive options.

They have discussed Chelsea's Axel Disasi as an alternative too, but that is now seen as unlikely. The Frenchman had interest from Roma also.

They have already added versatile Oscar Mingueza on a free after he left Celta Vigo.

Gunners get their man

Arsenal have completed the signing of winger Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge for £34million.

The fee is a record for the Belgian Pro League.

Arsenal have completed the signing of winger Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge for £34million

The 24-year-old, formerly of Norwich City, scored 17 goals and added 23 assists in 36 league appearances last season.

Magpies swoop for £30m star

Newcastle United have agreed a £35.5million deal for Monaco midfielder Aladji Bamba.

The 20-year-old travelled to Tyneside for a medical on Thursday morning ahead of completing his surprise move.

The France U20 international has only had one season in Monaco's first team and has made only 12 competitive starts in all competitions but is rated as an outstanding prospect.

The clubs have agreed an initial £30m guaranteed payment plus £5.5m in add-ons. There is also a 15 percent sell-on clause in the agreement.

Bamba, who plays as a defensive midfielder, made five Champions League appearances and 18 in Ligue Un last season.

Newcastle sold Sandro Tonali to Tottenham last month and have been in the market for a second young midfielder after signing 18-year-old Sean Steur from Ajax. Another target, Freiburg's Johan Manzambi, opted to join Aston Villa instead last week after they had agreed a £49m fee. They also enquired about Tottenham’s £50m-rated Lucas Bergvall but insist stopped short of a formal offer.

Newcastle United have agreed a deal to sign Monaco defensive midfielder Aladji Bamba (left)

It underlines a change in strategy for Newcastle of signing players to develop which carries a degree of risk. It also gives added importance to keeping experienced players such as Bruno Guimaraes though he remains eager to leave for Arsenal.

Newcastle remain the market for another goalkeeper after moving on from Manchester City's James Trafford, who is destined for Leeds.

They did hold a meeting over Brighton's Carl Rushworth who has been the subject of offers from Coventry City and was also on Leeds' radar.

🚨 Newcastle have agreed a £30m deal with AS Monaco for Aladji Bamba



✈️ The 20-yr-old midfielder is due on Tyneside this morning — Craig Hope (@CraigHope_DM) July 23, 2026

Saints stand firm on Charles fee

Southampton risk pricing Shea Charles out of a move to the Premier League as they push for over £30million for the Northern Ireland international.

Fulham are the latest club to be rebuffed after they offered in the region of £24million for the 22-year-old.

The Cottagers believed they could strike a deal on the understanding Saints would accept £25m plus add-ons. However, the Championship side are demanding more.

Charles, who they bought from Manchester City in 2023, made 38 appearances last season and scored what looked to be the winning goal in the play-off semi-final against Middlesbrough only for the club to be excluded from the showpiece Wembley final as a consequence of 'Spygate', as exclusively revealed by Daily Mail Sport.

Leeds United had made the early running for Charles.

They also made three offers to Southampton which were subsequently rejected and are likely to consider other options.

Manchester City also hold a 15percent sell-on.

Saints are trying to build for the new season against the backdrop of head coach Tonda Eckert facing a suspension after he was charged with misconduct by the Football Association for his role in the Spygate scandal. He had until Tuesday to respond to the charges.

West Brom are also keen on Saints forward Cameron Archer.

Leeds in talks with City over Trafford move

Leeds United are in talks to sign England international goalkeeper James Trafford from Manchester City.

Trafford, who went to the World Cup this summer, only rejoined Manchester City from Burnley last summer but managed just four Premier League outings.

Leeds are on the hunt for a new No 1 goalkeeper after Karl Darlow left for Manchester United.

Trafford came through City's academy but, after making no first-team appearances, left for Burnley in 2023 after a series of loans.

He rejoined last summer in a £31million deal - a record sum for a British goalkeeper.

As Daily Mail Sport reported in April, Trafford was back on Newcastle United's agenda to be their number one but they were aware it as becoming increasingly difficult amid competition and valuation last week.

Leeds are acting are losing Darlow. Illan Meslier has also joined Arsenal while Torino want Lucas Perri.

They have asked about Zion Suzuki at Parma but are hopeful Trafford will join as he looks to cement his place as Jordan Pickford's main rival to the England number one jersey.

Aston Villa and Spurs have also shown interest in Trafford but he sees an opportunity at Leeds to build his future.

Newcastle have also met Brighton goalkeeper Carl Rushworth’s representatives who remains subject of offers from Coventry City and was also on Leeds’ radar.

Leeds United are in talks to sign England international goalkeeper James Trafford (right)

Young Reds stopper leaves on loan

Liverpool goalkeeper Armin Pecsi has joined TSV Hartberg in Austria on a season-loan.

The 21-year-old, who made his senior international debut for Hungary last month, arrived at Anfield a year ago m.

He has been a regular for Liverpool's U21s and was also included in the senior side's matchday squad on five occasions.

Blues ramp up pursuit of Leverkusen teenager

Chelsea are stepping up their interest in Bayer Leverkusen winger Kerim Alajbegovic after offloading Alejandro Garnacho to Aston Villa and Nicolas Jackson expected to follow.

The exciting Bosnia international has had interest from Leeds United, Arsenal, Aston Villa and Atalanta.

Leverkusen sold the 18-year-old to Red Bull Salzburg last year but, after an impressive season, took up their option to buy him back this summer for £7million.

However, the winger made such an impression in Austria, and on World Cup duty with Bosnia, where he scored a spectacular long-range goal in their group-stage win over Qatar that his valuation is now closer to £30m.

Atalanta were considered to be in pole position earlier this month but Chelsea and Xabi Alonso were made aware of the opportunity and are now looking to strike a deal.

They have recognised the youngster's potential to add another pacy dimension to the first team set-up alongside new signing Morgan Rogers with Garnacho going and Nicolas Jackson expected to follow the Argentine to Villa.

Chelsea are stepping up their interest in Bayer Leverkusen winger Kerim Alajbegovic

Sports.title: White House defends Sophie Cunningham amid woke backlash... as WNBA star doubles down on trans views with new Instagram photos
Sports.content:
WNBA star Sophie Cunningham has received the backing of the White House after speaking on the trans athlete debate and insisting she wants to 'protect young girls'.

The 29-year-old underlined her support for the movement around protecting women's sports while talking with ESPN, saying women 'shouldn't have to go against biological men.'

Cunningham's words were inevitably picked up on and criticized online. WNBA fans have called for the league to ban or fine Cunningham for her remarks while many of the other responses on X have veered into abuse aimed at the Indiana Fever player.

However, amid the backlash, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt has now spoken out and offered her support to the Indiana Fever star.

'Men should not be playing in women's sports. It's completely ludicrous that anyone could support that,' Leavitt told reporters on Thursday.

'It's even more ludicrous that you do have Sophie Cunningham, a female athlete herself, very accomplished in her own right, coming forth and speaking that truth that men should(n't) play in women's sports.

Sophie Cunningham has spoken out about the debate about transgender athletes in sport

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt offered her support to the Indiana Fever star

'The backlash she is receiving from Democrats and left-wing figures across the country is astonishing. They are clearly very out of touch with the American public on this issue, which again, is an 80/20 issue. It's common sense.'

Meanwhile, Cunningham herself appeared to double down on her views with a not-so subtle Instagram post on Thursday afternoon.

Taking to the social media platform, the WNBA star shared pictures of her arriving before one of the Fever's recent games, with the caption: 'I said what I said.'

She also had the location tagged as 'Women's Sports', before later changing it.

Cunningham, who is a close friend to teammate Caitlin Clark, had already defended her comments before her team's Wednesday night game against Connecticut Sun.

She told reporters: 'There's going to be some negative comments but there's also a lot of positive comments too. It is what it is.

'We're all human, I really don't care what other people have to say. I said what I said, I think it's common sense and I think I will always believe in that. I stand on what I said.'

Cunningham was asked if her words signal a move to become more political but she denies having any aspirations to remain outspoken on any other major issues.

Cunningham doubled down after her comments about trans athletes sparked fury

The Indiana Fever star has become a fan-favorite in the WNBA over recent years

'I am not a very political person but I have beliefs, I have morals and I will always be true to who I am,' Cunningham said.

'I think people are going to take it how they want to take it. When it comes to protecting young girls and women in sports, I feel very strongly about that.'

The topic has become particularly politicized since President Donald Trump returned for a second term in office. He issued an executive order to block trans athletes participating in girls or women's sports and the Supreme Court recently upheld state bans on trans athletes.

Asked if her own comments could now 'come back' on the trans community, Cunningham said: 'I extend love, I don't dislike anyone.

'I think there's room for everyone here and there's room to love everyone. I truly think when you get people in the same room and you have conversations, you actually have a lot in common with a lot of people.

'I'm there to love but I am also there to love biological women and I think that there are rights that need to be protected. Like I said, I am going to stand true to that. I'll never falter in my beliefs for that.

Cunningham insisted that her comments are not hateful towards to the trans community

'But I've never said I hated the trans community. I think there is space for everyone.'

Back in 2022, Cunningham faced heavy backlash after sharing a post from CBS Sports host Josh Pate regarding the controversy surrounding former Penn transgender swimmer Lia Thomas and their inclusion on the women's team.

Pate's post read: 'Female collegiate athletes deserve so much better than this'.

Cunningham was forced to release a statement over the matter, at the time, saying that she 'stands' with athletes, but calling for 'fair' competition in events.

Sports.title: MALISHEVA 2 HIBERNIAN 0: Humiliation for Hibs as David Gray's Leith men fall to Kosovans in Conference League qualification
Sports.content:
Hibernian’s quest for Conference League football is in jeopardy after a humbling by unfancied Kosovan outfit Malisheva.

Kreshnik Uka stunned David Gray’s side in the first leg of the second qualifying tie at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium in Pristina when he opened the scoring in the 21st minute from close range.

Hibs stepped up the pressure after the break and new signing Nathan Lowe missed a couple of chances as they chased a precious equaliser but home substitute Valjmir Nafiu added a second in the 90th minute on the break to leave the Scots with a rescue mission in the second leg at Easter Road next week.

Gray and his men were roundly booed by the travelling fans who had made the journey to eastern Europe and the Hibs boss conceded they had let down their supporters.

And despite being second best throughout a miserable 90 minutes, the Easter Road boss insisted his men could turn the tie around in Leith next week.

‘We were way below the requirement and the expectations of this football club,’ conceded Gray. ‘I know that, and it’s a reflection on myself and the team.

Hibs defenders Felix Passlack and Adam Mayor reflect on a night to forget for the visitors

‘I’m not going to stand here and try and justify it or make excuses at all. We weren’t good enough.

‘The only positive, if there is anything to come out of today, is the fact it’s happened in the first leg and there is still an opportunity to turn it around — and I do believe we are good enough to do it from what I’ve seen today.

‘Fans will certainly not want to hear apologies. The support was incredible today. They have spent their money to come and watch the team and we know we’ve let them down.

‘I wasn’t shocked or surprised by anything I saw from the opposition, what we expected going into the game. We know that they’re an aggressive side, a team that will do the transition quickly — the second goal is another example of that.

‘Everything that could have gone wrong for us today certainly did and it’s very hard to win games of football when there’s so many of us not at the level required.

‘That wasn’t just one or two players. To win any game of football at any level, never mind European football, you need to have a level of performance that’s good enough throughout the team.

‘I don’t think there’s a single player today that can hold their hand up and say, I was at the very best of my ability today.

‘But I still firmly believe in the group. The criticism and everything is going to come and rightly so but there’s only one person who can try and turn it around and it’s my responsibility to make sure the team are right and ready for next week.’

Kreshnik Uka converts the opener to give the Kosovan side a deserved first-half lead

It was another abject night for Scottish football in Europe as the Leith side came up short against a club that is only a decade old.

On-loan Stoke striker Lowe was the only new signing in Gray’s side for the first competitive game of the season.

Hibs, who secured their European place with a fifth-placed finish in the Premiership last season, looked comfortable enough in the early stages in front of a sparse crowd.

In the seventh minute forward Owen Elding had a looping header from a Felix Passlack cross cleared off the line by Malisheva captain Dreni Kryeziu, with keeper Ilir Avdyli beaten.

The home side showed little in attack until the 15th minute when midfielder Arlind Veliu had an effort from inside the Hibs box deflected over the bar for a corner which came to nothing.

However, Malisheva kept pushing and when Veliu made his way down the left and cut the ball back into the box, Dzemal Ibishi missed the first contact but Uka stabbed the ball low past Hibs goalkeeper Raphael Sallinger.

Hibs’ response was lukewarm, notwithstanding a header from defender Grant Hanley that was easily saved by Avdyli.

Adam Mayor, Hibs’ summer signing from Millwall, replaced Jack Iredale for the second half and the Edinburgh side enjoyed more of the ball and put on some pressure.

Hibs boss David Gray remains confident his side can turn the tie around at Easter Road

Lowe, who scored in the win over Brondby last weekend, hit the outside of the post and went close again when he found himself through on goal in the 51st minute. Zambian midfielder Miguel Chaiwa soon blazed an effort over the bar following a corner.

The visitors kept pushing and in the 66th minute Lowe raced clear but missed the target with an unconvincing drive.

At the other end, Sallinger was pleased to see a header from Donart Vitija land in his arms.

The game became disjointed and scrappy in the final stages but Hibs were again stunned in the final minute of normal time when Nafiu fired high into the net after being brilliantly set up by Uka on the counter.

Gray’s side now have it all to do in the return game at home next week.

Malisheva (3-5-2): Avdyli; Shani (Murati 72), Kryeziu, Skovgaard; Isgandarli (Pira 72), Vitija (Luma 86), Ferati, Uka, Veliu; Ibishi (Bajraktari 92), Xhylani (Nafiu 71). Booked: None. Manager: Thomas Brdaric.

Hibernian (4-3-3): Sallinger; Passlack, O’Hora, Hanley, Iredale (Mayor 46); Mulligan (Abdulai 81), Chaiwa, Obita; Elding (Newell 68), Lowe, Boyle (Klidje 68). Booked: O’Hora, Abdulai. Manager: David Gray.

Sports.title: Donald Trump's Folarin Balogun red card intervention scandal takes fresh twist as match-fixing watchdog flags controversial reversal
Sports.content:
Donald Trump's Folarin Balogun red card intervention scandal takes fresh twist as match-fixing watchdog flags controversial reversal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A gambling watchdog group has flagged the United States' Round-of-16 loss to Belgium as one of seven World Cup matches that may have drawn irregular betting activity during the tournament.

Specifically, the independent Group of Copenhagen cited a predictions market line titled 'Will Folarin Balogun play against Belgium?' as one potential issue, sources told The Athletic.

That line opened on July 2 shortly after Balogun was given a controversial red card in Team USA's Round-of-32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina. On July 5, after President Donald Trump urged FIFA to rescind Balogun's red card, the governing body opted instead to suspend his one-game ban until after the tournament, thereby allowing him to play in the loss to Belgium.

Curiously, the Group of Copenhagen's report specified that no other similar markets opened for the 14 other players who got a red card during the tournament, according to The Athletic. Now the group has requested an official explanation from FIFA on the Balogun case.

The Daily Mail has sought comment from both FIFA and Polymarket, neither of which have been accused of any misconduct in this case.

Operating under the Council of Europe's Macolin Convention of 2014, the Group of Copenhagen is an independent network that detects and prevents the manipulation of sports competitions around the world. For the 2026 World Cup, the organization reviewed all 104 matches from the tournament, which attracted more than $240 billion bets worldwide, according to the Group of Copenhagen.

Folarin Balogun (20) fouls Bosnia's Tarik Muharemovic (4), resulting in a red card

Balogun was given a controversial red card in Team USA's Round-of-32 win over Bosnia

Although its full report has not yet been published, a summary of its conclusions has been shared by the Council of Europe.

The US loss to Belgium was among seven 'yellow notices' raised by the Group of Copenhagen, which has two higher levels of concern: orange and red.

'The Group of Copenhagen's notices can be explained by atypical behaviors such as changes in odds or hedging liquidities, there are many explanations that are not manipulations,' Christian Kalb, a gambling industry expert who previously worked with the Group of Copenhagen, told The Athletic.

'The major problem is when there may be a conflict of interest and potential inside information on those issues,' she continued. 'When we speak of prediction markets, we can detect some unusual behaviors but we must be very careful as they can be used for hedging markets.

The Norwegian FA is planning to complain to FIFA over the Folarin Balogun World Cup saga

Meanwhile, the Norwegian FA plans to launch a formal complaint to FIFA over Trump's interference in Balogun's red card ban.

Despite Trump's interventions, the US were thrashed 4-1 by Belgium, yet the 80-year-old has repeatedly boasted about his involvement, adding that FIFA President Gianni Infantino made a 'great decision.'

The antics of Trump and FIFA were widely condemned across the sport, and Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) President Lise Klaveness now says she is planning to formally complain to the governing body's ethics committee.

'When you bend a rule like this, you're on a slippery slope that will put the whole game at risk,' she said. 'It is a worry for the game when you compromise fundamental rules of the game.

'First of all, it should not have happened. It is very important now to have honest communication around it. We all know that this verdict was influenced from external forces and did not have the proper process.

'If you start to adapt in such a way towards state leaders and state politics, you will move your behavior and the organization's behavior, and also the red line of what states' leaders should interfere with. And that happened.'

Defending his role in the saga, Infantino insisted it was an independent decision taken by FIFA's disciplinary committee.

He said: 'They operate autonomously, apply the FIFA's disciplinary code, and decide cases based on the applicable regulations and the specific facts before them.

'Their independence is essential to the credibility and integrity of football, and this must always be respected.'

Sports.title: Jermain Defoe walks away from Woking after less than four months in charge: Ex-England star fails to take training before abruptly QUITTING amid clash with member of club management
Sports.content:
Jermain Defoe has walked away from National League Woking after just four months in charge.

Defoe managed six competitive matches at Woking and had been preparing the side for the new season but has abruptly quit his role.

Sources have told Daily Mail Sport that Defoe did not turn up to take training on Thursday and later called the club to inform them he would be stepping down.

One source indicated there was internal conflict between Defoe and a member of the Woking hierarchy. The National League club have declined to comment any further.

The former Spurs striker lost just one of his six games in charge, as the Surrey-based outfit finished tenth in the fifth tier.

In a statement, Woking said: ‘Woking Football Club can confirm that the club and First Team Manager Jermain Defoe have mutually agreed to part ways with immediate effect.

Jermain Defoe (left) has left his role as Woking manager after less than five months in charge

‘We would like to place on record our sincere thanks to Jermain for his contribution during his time at Woking Football Club, and we wish him every success in the future.

‘The club remains fully focused on delivering its objectives both on and off the pitch. We would like to thank our supporters for their continued support.’

Posting on Instagram, Defoe said: 'Following recent discussions, I can confirm that I have mutually agreed to leave my position as manager of Woking FC. Unfortunately, circumstances have ultimately made it impossible for me to continue in the position.

'I am extremely proud of the work undertaken during my time at the club and genuinely felt that we were building something special.

'I would like to thank Todd Johnson for giving me the opportunity to manage the club. I am incredibly grateful to the supporters and, most importantly, the players, who I am genuinely gutted for. The group is a fantastic one, and I wish the squad every success for the season ahead.

'Really disappointed the journey has ended so soon, but I leave with great pride in what Paul Bracewell, Karl Halabi and I were building at the club.

'My time at Woking FC has been an eye-opening managerial experience and one that will undoubtedly make me stronger for the next challenge in my career.’

Sports.title: 'Traumatic experience' - Kiwi sailing superstar sets sights on successful comeback in Portsmouth
Sports.content:
'Traumatic experience' - Kiwi sailing superstar sets sights on successful comeback in Portsmouth

The world's best sailors are descending on the south coast this weekend as the SailGP season continues.

View Image Women's Performance Session at SailGP Technologies ahead of the Emirates Great Britain Sail Grand Prix.

After their explosive start to the SailGP season was derailed by an enormous crash and a horror injury, Liv Mackay and Black Foils are hoping to hit the comeback trail at the Emirates Great Britain Sail Grand Prix in Portsmouth this weekend.

‌



The Kiwis lost control of their F50 in gusty conditions in front of their home crowd in Auckland, crashing into the French boat and leaving grinder Louis Sinclair with compound fractures in both legs following a sickening crash.

‌



But after their return to the water and competitive action last time out in Halifax, Canada, Mackay believes this weekend’s Portsmouth race – which will see the world's best athletes compete in close-to-shore, short races at speeds of more than 100km/h – can be the perfect reset.

‌



She said: “It was definitely the most traumatic experience I've ever had. There was a huge crowd, big grandstands, and it was obviously a home event. We'd been doing really well in the first two races and had a really good energy about it.

“But the crash itself was a loss of control of the boat, and we weren't able to regain that control on the breach. And unfortunately, when we did regain some sense of control we got hit. The whole experience was very short but long.

“Louis was stuck in the water and that was probably the most traumatic thing about all of it for quite some time. We were very fortunate that he didn't panic. He was very calm.”

‌



Thanks to months out with a broken boat, Black Foils currently sit 12th in the 13-team strong championship, leaving them targeting individual races rather than the overall standings.

But last year, they finished third across the championship, racking up more points than second placed Bonds Flying Roos, thanks to a memorable victory in Portsmouth.

Mackay said: “We're definitely a bit rusty when sailing together. But it's always a good feeling when you come back to where you won before, and it does bring back good memories, which is really nice.

‌



“There are a lot of Kiwis that live in England. A lot of my family's actually from England, so there are really strong ties here. The weather forecast is looking nice and windy, which is always fun. So yes, I'd say it's a pretty good feeling.”

The 30-year-old is the Black Foils’ strategist and competes alongside male counterparts in SailGP’s rare gender-integrated competition.

Emirates GBR may be the reigning world champions - and will be looking to get a home win in front of a sold-out crowd this weekend but the Kiwis have other ideas.

‌



Portsmouth is just about as far as you can get from Mackay’s childhood upbringing in rural New Zealand, but it won’t curb her enthusiasm in Portsmouth.

She said: “We are excited about this weekend, and we want to make our mark – we will be competitive.

“Most of our team members are actually from more rural parts of New Zealand. I definitely think it brings a different side to it, which is quite fun and makes us closer as a group.

Article continues below

“My parents didn't sail so my route into sailing was quite different to the typical one. I think it really shows my love for the sport. And my brother's the same. It's just a genuine journey. There's been no pressure.

“Our team is very proud of who we are as Kiwis. Being from different parts of New Zealand brings a unique team together.”

The Emirates Great Britain Sail Grand Prix returns to Portsmouth on 25-26 July. Limited tickets are still available via //SailGP.com/Portsmouth

Sports.title: Katarina Johnson-Thompson pulls out of Commonwealth Games as Team England reshuffles squad
Sports.content:
Katarina Johnson-Thompson pulls out of Commonwealth Games as Team England reshuffles squad

Katarina Johnson-Thompson's hopes of winning a historic third successive Commonwealth Games heptathlon title are over after the Team England star has opted to prioritise next month's European Athletics Championships instead.

View Image Katarina Johnson-Thompson will not defend her Commonwealth Games heptathlon title after withdrawing from Team England's squad.

Katarina Johnson-Thompson's bid for a historic third consecutive Commonwealth Games title is over before it has even begun. Johnson-Thompson is thought to have prioritised her bid for a first-ever European title in Birmingham next month and will be replaced by Niamh Emerson.

‌



The prospect of two home major championships in the space of a fortnight always meant difficult choices for British athletes. These Games were originally scheduled for March until Australia withdrew as hosts and Glasgow stepped in with just 18 months' notice.

‌



In addition to Johnson-Thompson, fellow Olympic medallists Dina Asher-Smith, Daryll Neita, Amber Anning and Matthew Hudson-Smith have all now confirmed they will miss the Games, with the team for the Europeans due to be named on Monday. Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson has always said Glasgow was not part of their plans for this season.

‌



Selection for Glasgow continues a remarkable comeback year for the 27-year-old Emerson, who completed her first heptathlon in eight years in April.

Emerson, who was previously mentored by Jessica Ennis-Hill, was tipped as the sport's next big thing after winning the world junior title in 2018, the same year she claimed Commonwealth bronze on the Gold Coast.

Asher-Smith is replaced by Renee Regis in the 4x100m relay squad, joining her sister Alicia, a member of the 4x400m team. Their selection comes 36 years after their father, John Regis, and mother, Jenny Stoute, both won Commonwealth gold in Auckland.

‌



"I wish the athletes the very best of luck in their recoveries and with the opportunities ahead during the rest of their seasons," said athletics team leader Scott Grace.

"This is a fantastic opportunity for athletes who are in excellent form to step into Team England and represent their country on the world stage. We are excited to support these athletes in Glasgow over the next couple of weeks."

Team England's athletics squad will now be headlined by world medallists Amy Hunt and Georgia Hunter Bell, who pulled out of last weekend's Diamond League meeting through illness.

‌



Hunt, who won 200m world silver in Tokyo, will compete in the 100m in Glasgow before doubling up in both sprint events in Birmingham.

"I think I'm always a bit of a dark horse going into championships, so no matter what's happened during my season, people should never write me off," said Hunt.

"At Christmas I wrote down my goals, and now I'm starting to think, 'Wow, maybe we can chase those.’"

Article continues below
